1.he: אִ֛ישׁ הָיָ֥ה בְאֶֽרֶץ־ע֖וּץ אִיּ֣וֹב שְׁמ֑וֹ וְהָיָ֣ה ׀ הָאִ֣ישׁ הַה֗וּא תָּ֧ם וְיָשָׁ֛ר וִירֵ֥א אֱלֹהִ֖ים וְסָ֥ר מֵרָֽע׃

lines.text: There was a man in the land of Uz, whose name was Job. That man was blameless and upright, and one who feared God, and turned away from evil.
A man there hath been in the land of Uz — Job his name — and that man hath been perfect and upright — both fearing God, and turning aside from evil.

1.he: וַיִּוָּ֥לְדוּ ל֛וֹ שִׁבְעָ֥ה בָנִ֖ים וְשָׁל֥וֹשׁ בָּנֽוֹת׃

lines.text: There were born to him seven sons and three daughters.
And there are borne to him seven sons and three daughters,

1.he: וַיְהִ֣י מִ֠קְנֵהוּ שִֽׁבְעַ֨ת אַלְפֵי־צֹ֜אן וּשְׁלֹ֧שֶׁת אַלְפֵ֣י גְמַלִּ֗ים וַחֲמֵ֨שׁ מֵא֤וֹת צֶֽמֶד־בָּקָר֙ וַחֲמֵ֣שׁ מֵא֣וֹת אֲתוֹנ֔וֹת וַעֲבֻדָּ֖ה רַבָּ֣ה מְאֹ֑ד וַיְהִי֙ הָאִ֣ישׁ הַה֔וּא גָּד֖וֹל מִכָּל־בְּנֵי־קֶֽדֶם׃

lines.text: His possessions also were seven thousand sheep, three thousand camels, five hundred yoke of oxen, five hundred female donkeys, and a very great household; so that this man was the greatest of all the children of the east.

and his substance is seven thousand sheep, and three thousand camels, and five hundred pairs of oxen, and five hundred she-asses, and a service very abundant; and that man is greater than any of the sons of the east.

1.he: וְהָלְכ֤וּ בָנָיו֙ וְעָשׂ֣וּ מִשְׁתֶּ֔ה בֵּ֖ית אִ֣ישׁ יוֹמ֑וֹ וְשָׁלְח֗וּ וְקָרְאוּ֙ לִשְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת אחיתיהם לֶאֱכֹ֥ל וְלִשְׁתּ֖וֹת עִמָּהֶֽם׃

lines.text: His sons went and held a feast in the house of each one on his birthday; and they sent and called for their three sisters to eat and to drink with them.
And his sons have gone and made a banquet — the house of each [in] his day — and have sent and called to their three sisters to eat and to drink with them;

1.he: וַיְהִ֡י כִּ֣י הִקִּיפֽוּ֩ יְמֵ֨י הַמִּשְׁתֶּ֜ה וַיִּשְׁלַ֧ח אִיּ֣וֹב וַֽיְקַדְּשֵׁ֗ם וְהִשְׁכִּ֣ים בַּבֹּקֶר֮ וְהֶעֱלָ֣ה עֹלוֹת֮ מִסְפַּ֣ר כֻּלָּם֒ כִּ֚י אָמַ֣ר אִיּ֔וֹב אוּלַי֙ חָטְא֣וּ בָנַ֔י וּבֵרֲכ֥וּ אֱלֹהִ֖ים בִּלְבָבָ֑ם כָּ֛כָה יַעֲשֶׂ֥ה אִיּ֖וֹב כָּל־הַיָּמִֽים׃

lines.text: It was so, when the days of their feasting had run their course, that Job sent and sanctified them, and rose up early in the morning, and offered burnt offerings according to the number of them all. For Job said, “It may be that my sons have sinned, and renounced God in their hearts.” Job did so continually.

and it cometh to pass, when they have gone round the days of the banquet, that Job doth send and sanctify them, and hath risen early in the morning, and caused to ascend burnt-offerings — the number of them all — for Job said, 'Perhaps my sons have sinned, yet blessed God in their heart.' Thus doth Job all the days.

1.he: וַיְהִ֣י הַיּ֔וֹם וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים לְהִתְיַצֵּ֖ב עַל־יְהוָ֑ה וַיָּב֥וֹא גַֽם־הַשָּׂטָ֖ן בְּתוֹכָֽם׃

lines.text: Now on the day when God’s sons came to present themselves before Yahweh, Satan also came among them.
And the day is, that sons of God come in to station themselves by Jehovah, and there doth come also the Adversary in their midst.

1.he: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר יְהוָ֛ה אֶל־הַשָּׂטָ֖ן מֵאַ֣יִן תָּבֹ֑א וַיַּ֨עַן הַשָּׂטָ֤ן אֶת־יְהוָה֙ וַיֹּאמַ֔ר מִשּׁ֣וּט בָּאָ֔רֶץ וּמֵֽהִתְהַלֵּ֖ךְ בָּֽהּ׃

lines.text: Yahweh said to Satan, “Where have you come from?” Then Satan answered Yahweh, and said, “From going back and forth in the earth, and from walking up and down in it.”
And Jehovah saith unto the Adversary, 'Whence comest thou?' And the Adversary answereth Jehovah and saith, 'From going to and fro in the land, and from walking up and down on it.'

1.he: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־הַשָּׂטָ֔ן הֲשַׂ֥מְתָּ לִבְּךָ֖ עַל־עַבְדִּ֣י אִיּ֑וֹב כִּ֣י אֵ֤ין כָּמֹ֨הוּ֙ בָּאָ֔רֶץ אִ֣ישׁ תָּ֧ם וְיָשָׁ֛ר יְרֵ֥א אֱלֹהִ֖ים וְסָ֥ר מֵרָֽע׃

lines.text: Yahweh said to Satan, “Have you considered my servant, Job? For there is no one like him in the earth, a blameless and an upright man, one who fears God, and turns away from evil.”
And Jehovah saith unto the Adversary, 'Hast thou set thy heart against My servant Job because there is none like him in the land, a man perfect and upright, fearing God, and turning aside from evil?'

1.he: וַיַּ֧עַן הַשָּׂטָ֛ן אֶת־יְהוָ֖ה וַיֹּאמַ֑ר הַֽחִנָּ֔ם יָרֵ֥א אִיּ֖וֹב אֱלֹהִֽים׃

lines.text: Then Satan answered Yahweh, and said, “Does Job fear God for nothing?
And the Adversary answereth Jehovah and saith, 'For nought is Job fearing God?

1.he: הֲלֹֽא־את שַׂ֣כְתָּ בַעֲד֧וֹ וּבְעַד־בֵּית֛וֹ וּבְעַ֥ד כָּל־אֲשֶׁר־ל֖וֹ מִסָּבִ֑יב מַעֲשֵׂ֤ה יָדָיו֙ בֵּרַ֔כְתָּ וּמִקְנֵ֖הוּ פָּרַ֥ץ בָּאָֽרֶץ׃

lines.text: Haven’t you made a hedge around him, and around his house, and around all that he has, on every side? You have blessed the work of his hands, and his substance is increased in the land.
Hast not Thou made a hedge for him, and for his house, and for all that he hath — round about?

1.he: וְאוּלָם֙ שְֽׁלַֽח־נָ֣א יָֽדְךָ֔ וְגַ֖ע בְּכָל־אֲשֶׁר־ל֑וֹ אִם־לֹ֥א עַל־פָּנֶ֖יךָ יְבָרֲכֶֽךָּ׃

lines.text: But stretch out your hand now, and touch all that he has, and he will renounce you to your face.”

The work of his hands Thou hast blessed, and his substance hath spread in the land, and yet, put forth, I pray Thee, Thy hand, and strike against anything that he hath — if not: to Thy face he doth bless Thee!'

1.he: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־הַשָּׂטָ֗ן הִנֵּ֤ה כָל־אֲשֶׁר־לוֹ֙ בְּיָדֶ֔ךָ רַ֣ק אֵלָ֔יו אַל־תִּשְׁלַ֖ח יָדֶ֑ךָ וַיֵּצֵא֙ הַשָּׂטָ֔ן מֵעִ֖ם פְּנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃

lines.text: Yahweh said to Satan, “Behold, all that he has is in your power. Only on himself don’t stretch out your hand.” So Satan went out from the presence of Yahweh.
And Jehovah saith unto the Adversary, 'Lo, all that he hath [is] in thy hand, only unto him put not forth thy hand.' And the Adversary goeth out from the presence of Jehovah.

1.he: וַיְהִ֖י הַיּ֑וֹם וּבָנָ֨יו וּבְנֹתָ֤יו אֹֽכְלִים֙ וְשֹׁתִ֣ים יַ֔יִן בְּבֵ֖ית אֲחִיהֶ֥ם הַבְּכֽוֹר׃

lines.text: It fell on a day when his sons and his daughters were eating and drinking wine in their oldest brother’s house,
And the day is, that his sons and his daughters are eating, and drinking wine, in the house of their brother, the first-born.

1.he: וּמַלְאָ֛ךְ בָּ֥א אֶל־אִיּ֖וֹב וַיֹּאמַ֑ר הַבָּקָר֙ הָי֣וּ חֹֽרְשׁ֔וֹת וְהָאֲתֹנ֖וֹת רֹע֥וֹת עַל־יְדֵיהֶֽם׃

lines.text: that there came a messenger to Job, and said, “The oxen were plowing, and the donkeys feeding beside them,
And a messenger hath come in unto Job and saith, 'The oxen have been plowing, and the she-asses feeding by their sides,

1.he: וַתִּפֹּ֤ל שְׁבָא֙ וַתִּקָּחֵ֔ם וְאֶת־הַנְּעָרִ֖ים הִכּ֣וּ לְפִי־חָ֑רֶב וָֽאִמָּ֨לְטָ֧ה רַק־אֲנִ֛י לְבַדִּ֖י לְהַגִּ֥יד לָֽךְ׃

lines.text: and the Sabeans attacked, and took them away. Yes, they have killed the servants with the edge of the sword, and I alone have escaped to tell you.”
and Sheba doth fall, and take them, and the young men they have smitten by the mouth of the sword, and I am escaped — only I alone — to declare [it] to thee.'

1.he: ע֣וֹד ׀ זֶ֣ה מְדַבֵּ֗ר וְזֶה֮ בָּ֣א וַיֹּאמַר֒ אֵ֣שׁ אֱלֹהִ֗ים נָֽפְלָה֙ מִן־הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וַתִּבְעַ֥ר בַּצֹּ֛אן וּבַנְּעָרִ֖ים וַתֹּאכְלֵ֑ם וָאִמָּ֨לְטָ֧ה רַק־אֲנִ֛י לְבַדִּ֖י לְהַגִּ֥יד לָֽךְ׃

lines.text: While he was still speaking, there also came another, and said, “The fire of God has fallen from the sky, and has burned up the sheep and the servants, and consumed them, and I alone have escaped to tell you.”

While this [one] is speaking another also hath come and saith, 'Fire of God hath fallen from the heavens, and burneth among the flock, and among the young men, and consumeth them, and I am escaped — only I alone — to declare [it] to thee.'

1.he: ע֣וֹד ׀ זֶ֣ה מְדַבֵּ֗ר וְזֶה֮ בָּ֣א וַיֹּאמַר֒ כַּשְׂדִּ֞ים שָׂ֣מוּ ׀ שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה רָאשִׁ֗ים וַֽיִּפְשְׁט֤וּ עַל־הַגְּמַלִּים֙ וַיִּקָּח֔וּם וְאֶת־הַנְּעָרִ֖ים הִכּ֣וּ לְפִי־חָ֑רֶב וָאִמָּ֨לְטָ֧ה רַק־אֲנִ֛י לְבַדִּ֖י לְהַגִּ֥יד לָֽךְ׃

lines.text: While he was still speaking, there came also another, and said, “The Chaldeans made three bands, and swept down on the camels, and have taken them away, yes, and killed the servants with the edge of the sword; and I alone have escaped to tell you.”

While this [one] is speaking another also hath come and saith, 'Chaldeans made three heads, and rush on the camels, and take them, and the young men they have smitten by the mouth of the sword, and I am escaped — only I alone — to declare [it] to thee.'

1.he: עַ֚ד זֶ֣ה מְדַבֵּ֔ר וְזֶ֖ה בָּ֣א וַיֹּאמַ֑ר בָּנֶ֨יךָ וּבְנוֹתֶ֤יךָ אֹֽכְלִים֙ וְשֹׁתִ֣ים יַ֔יִן בְּבֵ֖ית אֲחִיהֶ֥ם הַבְּכֽוֹר׃

lines.text: While he was still speaking, there came also another, and said, “Your sons and your daughters were eating and drinking wine in their oldest brother’s house,
While this [one] is speaking another also hath come and saith, 'Thy sons and thy daughters are eating, and drinking wine, in the house of their brother, the first-born.

1.he: וְהִנֵּה֩ ר֨וּחַ גְּדוֹלָ֜ה בָּ֣אָה ׀ מֵעֵ֣בֶר הַמִּדְבָּ֗ר וַיִּגַּע֙ בְּאַרְבַּע֙ פִּנּ֣וֹת הַבַּ֔יִת וַיִּפֹּ֥ל עַל־הַנְּעָרִ֖ים וַיָּמ֑וּתוּ וָאִמָּ֨לְטָ֧ה רַק־אֲנִ֛י לְבַדִּ֖י לְהַגִּ֥יד לָֽךְ׃

lines.text: and behold, there came a great wind from the wilderness, and struck the four corners of the house, and it fell on the young men, and they are dead. I alone have escaped to tell you.”

And lo, a great wind hath come from over the wilderness, and striketh against the four corners of the house, and it falleth on the young men, and they are dead, and I am escaped — only I alone — to declare [it] to thee.'

1.he: וַיָּ֤קָם אִיּוֹב֙ וַיִּקְרַ֣ע אֶת־מְעִל֔וֹ וַיָּ֖גָז אֶת־רֹאשׁ֑וֹ וַיִּפֹּ֥ל אַ֖רְצָה וַיִּשְׁתָּֽחוּ׃

lines.text: Then Job arose, and tore his robe, and shaved his head, and fell down on the ground, and worshiped.
And Job riseth, and rendeth his robe, and shaveth his head, and falleth to the earth, and doth obeisance,

1.he: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ עָרֹ֨ם יצתי מִבֶּ֣טֶן אִמִּ֗י וְעָרֹם֙ אָשׁ֣וּב שָׁ֔מָה יְהוָ֣ה נָתַ֔ן וַיהוָ֖ה לָקָ֑ח יְהִ֛י שֵׁ֥ם יְהוָ֖ה מְבֹרָֽךְ׃

lines.text: He said, “Naked I came out of my mother’s womb, and naked will I return there. Yahweh gave, and Yahweh has taken away. Blessed be Yahweh’s name.”
and he saith, 'Naked came I forth from the womb of my mother, and naked I turn back thither: Jehovah hath given and Jehovah hath taken: let the name of Jehovah be blessed.'

1.he: בְּכָל־זֹ֖את לֹא־חָטָ֣א אִיּ֑וֹב וְלֹא־נָתַ֥ן תִּפְלָ֖ה לֵאלֹהִֽים׃

lines.text: In all this, Job didn’t sin, nor charge God with wrongdoing.
In all this Job hath not sinned, nor given folly to God.

2.he: וַיְהִ֣י הַיּ֔וֹם וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים לְהִתְיַצֵּ֖ב עַל־יְהוָ֑ה וַיָּב֤וֹא גַֽם־הַשָּׂטָן֙ בְּתֹכָ֔ם לְהִתְיַצֵּ֖ב עַל־יְהוָֽה׃

lines.text: Again, on the day when the God’s sons came to present themselves before Yahweh, Satan came also among them to present himself before Yahweh.
And the day is, that sons of God come in to station themselves by Jehovah, and there doth come also the Adversary in their midst to station himself by Jehovah.

2.he: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־הַשָּׂטָ֔ן אֵ֥י מִזֶּ֖ה תָּבֹ֑א וַיַּ֨עַן הַשָּׂטָ֤ן אֶת־יְהוָה֙ וַיֹּאמַ֔ר מִשֻּׁ֣ט בָּאָ֔רֶץ וּמֵהִתְהַלֵּ֖ךְ בָּֽהּ׃

lines.text: Yahweh said to Satan, “Where have you come from?” Satan answered Yahweh, and said, “From going back and forth in the earth, and from walking up and down in it.”
And Jehovah saith unto the Adversary, 'Whence camest thou?' And the Adversary answereth Jehovah and saith, 'From going to and fro in the land, and from walking up and down in it.'

2.he: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־הַשָּׂטָ֗ן הֲשַׂ֣מְתָּ לִבְּךָ֮ אֶל־עַבְדִּ֣י אִיּוֹב֒ כִּי֩ אֵ֨ין כָּמֹ֜הוּ בָּאָ֗רֶץ אִ֣ישׁ תָּ֧ם וְיָשָׁ֛ר יְרֵ֥א אֱלֹהִ֖ים וְסָ֣ר מֵרָ֑ע וְעֹדֶ֨נּוּ֙ מַחֲזִ֣יק בְּתֻמָּת֔וֹ וַתְּסִיתֵ֥נִי ב֖וֹ לְבַלְּע֥וֹ חִנָּֽם׃

lines.text: Yahweh said to Satan, “Have you considered my servant Job? For there is no one like him in the earth, a blameless and an upright man, one who fears God, and turns away from evil. He still maintains his integrity, although you incited me against him, to ruin him without cause.”

And Jehovah saith unto the Adversary, 'Hast thou set thy heart unto My servant Job because there is none like him in the land, a man perfect and upright, fearing God and turning aside from evil? and still he is keeping hold on his integrity, and thou dost move Me against him to swallow him up for nought!'

2.he: וַיַּ֧עַן הַשָּׂטָ֛ן אֶת־יְהוָ֖ה וַיֹּאמַ֑ר ע֣וֹר בְּעַד־ע֗וֹר וְכֹל֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לָאִ֔ישׁ יִתֵּ֖ן בְּעַ֥ד נַפְשֽׁוֹ׃

lines.text: Satan answered Yahweh, and said, “Skin for skin. Yes, all that a man has he will give for his life.
And the Adversary answereth Jehovah and saith, 'A skin for a skin, and all that a man hath he doth give for his life.

2.he: אוּלָם֙ שְֽׁלַֽח־נָ֣א יָֽדְךָ֔ וְגַ֥ע אֶל־עַצְמ֖וֹ וְאֶל־בְּשָׂר֑וֹ אִם־לֹ֥א אֶל־פָּנֶ֖יךָ יְבָרֲכֶֽךָּ׃

lines.text: But stretch out your hand now, and touch his bone and his flesh, and he will renounce you to your face.”
Yet, put forth, I pray Thee, Thy hand, and strike unto his bone and unto his flesh — if not: unto Thy face he doth bless Thee!'

2.he: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר יְהוָ֛ה אֶל־הַשָּׂטָ֖ן הִנּ֣וֹ בְיָדֶ֑ךָ אַ֖ךְ אֶת־נַפְשׁ֥וֹ שְׁמֹֽר׃

lines.text: Yahweh said to Satan, “Behold, he is in your hand. Only spare his life.”
And Jehovah saith unto the Adversary, 'Lo, he [is] in thy hand; only his life take care of.'

2.he: וַיֵּצֵא֙ הַשָּׂטָ֔ן מֵאֵ֖ת פְּנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַיַּ֤ךְ אֶת־אִיּוֹב֙ בִּשְׁחִ֣ין רָ֔ע מִכַּ֥ף רַגְל֖וֹ עד קָדְקֳדֽוֹ׃

lines.text: So Satan went out from the presence of Yahweh, and struck Job with painful sores from the sole of his foot to his head.
And the Adversary goeth forth from the presence of Jehovah, and smiteth Job with a sore ulcer from the sole of his foot unto his crown.

2.he: וַיִּֽקַּֽח־ל֣וֹ חֶ֔רֶשׂ לְהִתְגָּרֵ֖ד בּ֑וֹ וְה֖וּא יֹשֵׁ֥ב בְּתוֹךְ־הָאֵֽפֶר׃

lines.text: He took for himself a potsherd to scrape himself with, and he sat among the ashes.
And he taketh to him a potsherd to scrape himself with it, and he is sitting in the midst of the ashes.

2.he: וַתֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ אִשְׁתּ֔וֹ עֹדְךָ֖ מַחֲזִ֣יק בְּתֻמָּתֶ֑ךָ בָּרֵ֥ךְ אֱלֹהִ֖ים וָמֻֽת׃

lines.text: Then his wife said to him, “Do you still maintain your integrity? Renounce God, and die.”
And his wife saith to him, 'Still thou art keeping hold on thine integrity: bless God and die.'

2.he: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלֶ֗יהָ כְּדַבֵּ֞ר אַחַ֤ת הַנְּבָלוֹת֙ תְּדַבֵּ֔רִי גַּ֣ם אֶת־הַטּ֗וֹב נְקַבֵּל֙ מֵאֵ֣ת הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים וְאֶת־הָרָ֖ע לֹ֣א נְקַבֵּ֑ל בְּכָל־זֹ֛את לֹא־חָטָ֥א אִיּ֖וֹב בִּשְׂפָתָֽיו׃

lines.text: But he said to her, “You speak as one of the foolish women would speak. What? Shall we receive good at the hand of God, and shall we not receive evil?” In all this Job didn’t sin with his lips.
And he saith unto her, 'As one of the foolish women speaketh, thou speakest; yea, the good we receive from God, and the evil we do not receive.' In all this Job hath not sinned with his lips.

2.he: וַֽיִּשְׁמְע֞וּ שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת ׀ רֵעֵ֣י אִיּ֗וֹב אֵ֣ת כָּל־הָרָעָ֣ה הַזֹּאת֮ הַבָּ֣אָה עָלָיו֒ וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ֙ אִ֣ישׁ מִמְּקֹמ֔וֹ אֱלִיפַ֤ז הַתֵּימָנִי֙ וּבִלְדַּ֣ד הַשּׁוּחִ֔י וְצוֹפַ֖ר הַנַּֽעֲמָתִ֑י וַיִּוָּעֲד֣וּ יַחְדָּ֔ו לָב֥וֹא לָנֽוּד־ל֖וֹ וּֽלְנַחֲמֽוֹ׃

lines.text: Now when Job’s three friends heard of all this evil that had come on him, they each came from his own place: Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite; and they made an appointment together to come to sympathize with him and to comfort him.

And three of the friends of Job hear of all this evil that hath come upon him, and they come in each from his place — Eliphaz the Temanite, and Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite — and they are met together to come in to bemoan him, and to comfort him;

2.he: וַיִּשְׂא֨וּ אֶת־עֵינֵיהֶ֤ם מֵרָחוֹק֙ וְלֹ֣א הִכִּירֻ֔הוּ וַיִּשְׂא֥וּ קוֹלָ֖ם וַיִּבְכּ֑וּ וַֽיִּקְרְעוּ֙ אִ֣ישׁ מְעִל֔וֹ וַיִּזְרְק֥וּ עָפָ֛ר עַל־רָאשֵׁיהֶ֖ם הַשָּׁמָֽיְמָה׃

lines.text: When they lifted up their eyes from a distance, and didn’t recognize him, they raised their voices, and wept; and they each tore his robe, and sprinkled dust on their heads toward the sky.
and they lift up their eyes from afar and have not discerned him, and they lift up their voice and weep, and rend each his robe, and sprinkle dust on their heads — heavenward.

2.he: וַיֵּשְׁב֤וּ אִתּוֹ֙ לָאָ֔רֶץ שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִ֖ים וְשִׁבְעַ֣ת לֵיל֑וֹת וְאֵין־דֹּבֵ֤ר אֵלָיו֙ דָּבָ֔ר כִּ֣י רָא֔וּ כִּֽי־גָדַ֥ל הַכְּאֵ֖ב מְאֹֽד׃

lines.text: So they sat down with him on the ground seven days and seven nights, and no one spoke a word to him, for they saw that his grief was very great.
And they sit with him on the earth seven days and seven nights, and there is none speaking unto him a word when they have seen that the pain hath been very great.

3.he: אַחֲרֵי־כֵ֗ן פָּתַ֤ח אִיּוֹב֙ אֶת־פִּ֔יהוּ וַיְקַלֵּ֖ל אֶת־יוֹמֽוֹ׃

lines.text: After this Job opened his mouth, and cursed the day of his birth.
After this hath Job opened his mouth, and revileth his day.

3.he: וַיַּ֥עַן אִיּ֗וֹב וַיֹּאמַֽר׃

lines.text: Job answered:
And Job answereth and saith: —

3.he: יֹ֣אבַד י֭וֹם אִוָּ֣לֶד בּ֑וֹ וְהַלַּ֥יְלָה אָ֝מַ֗ר הֹ֣רָה גָֽבֶר׃

lines.text: “Let the day perish in which I was born, the night which said, ‘There is a boy conceived.’
Let the day perish in which I am born, And the night that hath said: 'A man-child hath been conceived.'

3.he: הַיּ֥וֹם הַה֗וּא יְֽהִ֫י חֹ֥שֶׁךְ אַֽל־יִדְרְשֵׁ֣הוּ אֱל֣וֹהַּ מִמָּ֑עַל וְאַל־תּוֹפַ֖ע עָלָ֣יו נְהָרָֽה׃

lines.text: Let that day be darkness. Don’t let God from above seek for it, neither let the light shine on it.
That day — let it be darkness, Let not God require it from above, Nor let light shine upon it.

3.he: יִגְאָלֻ֡הוּ חֹ֣שֶׁךְ וְ֭צַלְמָוֶת תִּשְׁכָּן־עָלָ֣יו עֲנָנָ֑ה יְ֝בַעֲתֻ֗הוּ כִּֽמְרִ֥ירֵי יֽוֹם׃

lines.text: Let darkness and the shadow of death claim it for their own. Let a cloud dwell on it. Let all that makes black the day terrify it.
Let darkness and death-shade redeem it, Let a cloud tabernacle upon it, Let them terrify it as the most bitter of days.

3.he: הַלַּ֥יְלָה הַהוּא֮ יִקָּחֵ֪ה֫וּ אֹ֥פֶל אַל־יִ֭חַדְּ בִּימֵ֣י שָׁנָ֑ה בְּמִסְפַּ֥ר יְ֝רָחִ֗ים אַל־יָבֹֽא׃

lines.text: As for that night, let thick darkness seize on it. Let it not rejoice among the days of the year. Let it not come into the number of the months.
That night — let thick darkness take it, Let it not be united to days of the year, Into the number of months let it not come.

3.he: הִנֵּ֤ה הַלַּ֣יְלָה הַ֭הוּא יְהִ֣י גַלְמ֑וּד אַל־תָּבֹ֖א רְנָנָ֣ה בֽוֹ׃

lines.text: Behold, let that night be barren. Let no joyful voice come therein.
Lo! that night — let it be gloomy, Let no singing come into it.

3.he: יִקְּבֻ֥הוּ אֹרְרֵי־י֑וֹם הָ֝עֲתִידִ֗ים עֹרֵ֥ר לִוְיָתָֽן׃

lines.text: Let them curse it who curse the day, who are ready to rouse up leviathan.
Let the cursers of day mark it, Who are ready to wake up Leviathan.

3.he: יֶחְשְׁכוּ֮ כּוֹכְבֵ֪י נִ֫שְׁפּ֥וֹ יְקַו־לְא֥וֹר וָאַ֑יִן וְאַל־יִ֝רְאֶ֗ה בְּעַפְעַפֵּי־שָֽׁחַר׃

lines.text: Let the stars of its twilight be dark. Let it look for light, but have none, neither let it see the eyelids of the morning,
Let the stars of its twilight be dark, Let it wait for light, and there is none, And let it not look on the eyelids of the dawn.

3.he: כִּ֤י לֹ֣א סָ֭גַר דַּלְתֵ֣י בִטְנִ֑י וַיַּסְתֵּ֥ר עָ֝מָ֗ל מֵעֵינָֽי׃

lines.text: because it didn’t shut up the doors of my mother’s womb, nor did it hide trouble from my eyes.
Because it hath not shut the doors Of the womb that was mine! And hide misery from mine eyes.

3.he: לָ֤מָּה לֹּ֣א מֵרֶ֣חֶם אָמ֑וּת מִבֶּ֖טֶן יָצָ֣אתִי וְאֶגְוָֽע׃

lines.text: “Why didn’t I die from the womb? Why didn’t I give up the spirit when my mother bore me?
Why from the womb do I not die? From the belly I have come forth and gasp!

3.he: מַ֭דּוּעַ קִדְּמ֣וּנִי בִרְכָּ֑יִם וּמַה־שָּׁ֝דַ֗יִם כִּ֣י אִינָֽק׃

lines.text: Why did the knees receive me? Or why the breast, that I should nurse?
Wherefore have knees been before me? And what [are] breasts, that I suck?

3.he: כִּֽי־עַ֭תָּה שָׁכַ֣בְתִּי וְאֶשְׁק֑וֹט יָ֝שַׁ֗נְתִּי אָ֤ז ׀ יָנ֬וּחַֽ לִֽי׃

lines.text: For now should I have lain down and been quiet. I should have slept, then I would have been at rest,
For now, I have lain down, and am quiet, I have slept — then there is rest to me,

3.he: עִם־מְ֭לָכִים וְיֹ֣עֲצֵי אָ֑רֶץ הַבֹּנִ֖ים חֳרָב֣וֹת לָֽמוֹ׃

lines.text: with kings and counselors of the earth, who built up waste places for themselves;
With kings and counsellors of earth, These building wastes for themselves.

3.he: א֣וֹ עִם־שָׂ֭רִים זָהָ֣ב לָהֶ֑ם הַֽמְמַלְאִ֖ים בָּתֵּיהֶ֣ם כָּֽסֶף׃

lines.text: or with princes who had gold, who filled their houses with silver:
Or with princes — they have gold, They are filling their houses [with] silver.

3.he: א֤וֹ כְנֵ֣פֶל טָ֭מוּן לֹ֣א אֶהְיֶ֑ה כְּ֝עֹלְלִ֗ים לֹא־רָ֥אוּ אֽוֹר׃

lines.text: or as a hidden untimely birth I had not been, as infants who never saw light.
(Or as a hidden abortion I am not, As infants — they have not seen light.)

3.he: שָׁ֣ם רְ֭שָׁעִים חָ֣דְלוּ רֹ֑גֶז וְשָׁ֥ם יָ֝נ֗וּחוּ יְגִ֣יעֵי כֹֽחַ׃

lines.text: There the wicked cease from troubling. There the weary are at rest.
There the wicked have ceased troubling, And there rest do the wearied in power.

3.he: יַ֭חַד אֲסִירִ֣ים שַׁאֲנָ֑נוּ לֹ֥א שָׁ֝מְע֗וּ ק֣וֹל נֹגֵֽשׂ׃

lines.text: There the prisoners are at ease together. They don’t hear the voice of the taskmaster.
Together prisoners have been at ease, They have not heard the voice of an exactor,

3.he: קָטֹ֣ן וְ֭גָדוֹל שָׁ֣ם ה֑וּא וְ֝עֶ֗בֶד חָפְשִׁ֥י מֵאֲדֹנָֽיו׃

lines.text: The small and the great are there. The servant is free from his master.
Small and great [are] there the same. And a servant [is] free from his lord.

3.he: לָ֤מָּה יִתֵּ֣ן לְעָמֵ֣ל א֑וֹר וְ֝חַיִּ֗ים לְמָ֣רֵי נָֽפֶשׁ׃

lines.text: “Why is light given to him who is in misery, life to the bitter in soul,
Why giveth He to the miserable light, and life to the bitter soul?

3.he: הַֽמְחַכִּ֣ים לַמָּ֣וֶת וְאֵינֶ֑נּוּ וַֽ֝יַּחְפְּרֻ֗הוּ מִמַּטְמוֹנִֽים׃

lines.text: Who long for death, but it doesn’t come; and dig for it more than for hidden treasures,
Who are waiting for death, and it is not, And they seek it above hid treasures.

3.he: הַשְּׂמֵחִ֥ים אֱלֵי־גִ֑יל יָ֝שִׂ֗ישׂוּ כִּ֣י יִמְצְאוּ־קָֽבֶר׃

lines.text: who rejoice exceedingly, and are glad, when they can find the grave?
Who are glad — unto joy, They rejoice when they find a grave.

3.he: לְ֭גֶבֶר אֲשֶׁר־דַּרְכּ֣וֹ נִסְתָּ֑רָה וַיָּ֖סֶךְ אֱל֣וֹהַּ בַּעֲדֽוֹ׃

lines.text: Why is light given to a man whose way is hidden, whom God has hedged in?
To a man whose way hath been hidden, And whom God doth shut up?

3.he: כִּֽי־לִפְנֵ֣י לַ֭חְמִי אַנְחָתִ֣י תָבֹ֑א וַֽיִּתְּכ֥וּ כַ֝מַּ֗יִם שַׁאֲגֹתָֽי׃

lines.text: For my sighing comes before I eat. My groanings are poured out like water.
For before my food, my sighing cometh, And poured out as waters [are] my roarings.

3.he: כִּ֤י פַ֣חַד פָּ֭חַדְתִּי וַיֶּאֱתָיֵ֑נִי וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר יָ֝גֹ֗רְתִּי יָ֣בֹא לִֽי׃

lines.text: For the thing which I fear comes on me, That which I am afraid of comes to me.
For a fear I feared and it meeteth me, And what I was afraid of doth come to me.

3.he: לֹ֤א שָׁלַ֨וְתִּי ׀ וְלֹ֖א שָׁקַ֥טְתִּי וְֽלֹא־נָ֗חְתִּי וַיָּ֥בֹא רֹֽגֶז׃

lines.text: I am not at ease, neither am I quiet, neither have I rest; but trouble comes.”
I was not safe — nor was I quiet — Nor was I at rest — and trouble cometh!

4.he: וַ֭יַּעַן אֱלִיפַ֥ז הַֽתֵּימָנִ֗י וַיֹּאמַֽר׃

lines.text: Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered,
And Eliphaz the Temanite answereth and saith: —

4.he: הֲנִסָּ֬ה דָבָ֣ר אֵלֶ֣יךָ תִּלְאֶ֑ה וַעְצֹ֥ר בְּ֝מִלִּ֗ין מִ֣י יוּכָֽל׃

lines.text: “If someone ventures to talk with you, will you be grieved? But who can withhold himself from speaking?
Hath one tried a word with thee? — Thou art weary! And to keep in words who is able?

4.he: הִ֭נֵּה יִסַּ֣רְתָּ רַבִּ֑ים וְיָדַ֖יִם רָפ֣וֹת תְּחַזֵּֽק׃

lines.text: Behold, you have instructed many, you have strengthened the weak hands.
Lo, thou hast instructed many, And feeble hands thou makest strong.

4.he: כּ֭וֹשֵׁל יְקִימ֣וּן מִלֶּ֑יךָ וּבִרְכַּ֖יִם כֹּרְע֣וֹת תְּאַמֵּֽץ׃

lines.text: Your words have supported him who was falling, You have made firm the feeble knees.
The stumbling one do thy words raise up, And bowing knees thou dost strengthen.

4.he: כִּ֤י עַתָּ֨ה ׀ תָּב֣וֹא אֵלֶ֣יךָ וַתֵּ֑לֶא תִּגַּ֥ע עָ֝דֶ֗יךָ וַתִּבָּהֵֽל׃

lines.text: But now it has come to you, and you faint. It touches you, and you are troubled.
But now, it cometh in unto thee, And thou art weary; It striketh unto thee, and thou art troubled.

4.he: הֲלֹ֣א יִ֭רְאָתְךָ כִּסְלָתֶ֑ךָ תִּ֝קְוָתְךָ֗ וְתֹ֣ם דְּרָכֶֽיךָ׃

lines.text: Isn’t your piety your confidence? Isn’t the integrity of your ways your hope?
Is not thy reverence thy confidence? Thy hope — the perfection of thy ways?

4.he: זְכָר־נָ֗א מִ֤י ה֣וּא נָקִ֣י אָבָ֑ד וְ֝אֵיפֹ֗ה יְשָׁרִ֥ים נִכְחָֽדוּ׃

lines.text: “Remember, now, whoever perished, being innocent? Or where were the upright cut off?
Remember, I pray thee, Who, being innocent, hath perished? And where have the upright been cut off?

4.he: כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר רָ֭אִיתִי חֹ֣רְשֵׁי אָ֑וֶן וְזֹרְעֵ֖י עָמָ֣ל יִקְצְרֻֽהוּ׃

lines.text: According to what I have seen, those who plow iniquity, and sow trouble, reap the same.
As I have seen — ploughers of iniquity, And sowers of misery, reap it!

4.he: מִנִּשְׁמַ֣ת אֱל֣וֹהַ יֹאבֵ֑דוּ וּמֵר֖וּחַ אַפּ֣וֹ יִכְלֽוּ׃

lines.text: By the breath of God they perish. By the blast of his anger are they consumed.
From the breath of God they perish, And from the spirit of His anger consumed.

4.he: שַׁאֲגַ֣ת אַ֭רְיֵה וְק֣וֹל שָׁ֑חַל וְשִׁנֵּ֖י כְפִירִ֣ים נִתָּֽעוּ׃

lines.text: The roaring of the lion, and the voice of the fierce lion, the teeth of the young lions, are broken.
The roaring of a lion, And the voice of a fierce lion, And teeth of young lions have been broken.

4.he: לַ֭יִשׁ אֹבֵ֣ד מִבְּלִי־טָ֑רֶף וּבְנֵ֥י לָ֝בִ֗יא יִתְפָּרָֽדוּ׃

lines.text: The old lion perishes for lack of prey. The cubs of the lioness are scattered abroad.
An old lion is perishing without prey, And the whelps of the lioness do separate.

4.he: וְ֭אֵלַי דָּבָ֣ר יְגֻנָּ֑ב וַתִּקַּ֥ח אָ֝זְנִ֗י שֵׁ֣מֶץ מֶֽנְהֽוּ׃

lines.text: “Now a thing was secretly brought to me. My ear received a whisper of it.
And unto me a thing is secretly brought, And receive doth mine ear a little of it.

4.he: בִּ֭שְׂעִפִּים מֵחֶזְיֹנ֣וֹת לָ֑יְלָה בִּנְפֹ֥ל תַּ֝רְדֵּמָ֗ה עַל־אֲנָשִֽׁים׃

lines.text: In thoughts from the visions of the night, when deep sleep falls on men,
In thoughts from visions of the night, In the falling of deep sleep on men,

4.he: פַּ֣חַד קְ֭רָאַנִי וּרְעָדָ֑ה וְרֹ֖ב עַצְמוֹתַ֣י הִפְחִֽיד׃

lines.text: fear came on me, and trembling, which made all my bones shake.
Fear hath met me, and trembling, And the multitude of my bones caused to fear.

4.he: וְ֭רוּחַ עַל־פָּנַ֣י יַחֲלֹ֑ף תְּ֝סַמֵּ֗ר שַֽׂעֲרַ֥ת בְּשָׂרִֽי׃

lines.text: Then a spirit passed before my face. The hair of my flesh stood up.
And a spirit before my face doth pass, Stand up doth the hair of my flesh;

4.he: יַעֲמֹ֤ד ׀ וְֽלֹא־אַכִּ֬יר מַרְאֵ֗הוּ תְּ֭מוּנָה לְנֶ֣גֶד עֵינָ֑י דְּמָמָ֖ה וָק֣וֹל אֶשְׁמָֽע׃

lines.text: It stood still, but I couldn’t discern its appearance. A form was before my eyes. Silence, then I heard a voice, saying,
It standeth, and I discern not its aspect, A similitude [is] over-against mine eyes, Silence! and a voice I hear:

4.he: הַֽ֭אֱנוֹשׁ מֵאֱל֣וֹהַ יִצְדָּ֑ק אִ֥ם מֵ֝עֹשֵׂ֗הוּ יִטְהַר־גָּֽבֶר׃

lines.text: ‘Shall mortal man be more just than God? Shall a man be more pure than his Maker?
'Is mortal man than God more righteous? Than his Maker is a man cleaner?

4.he: הֵ֣ן בַּ֭עֲבָדָיו לֹ֣א יַאֲמִ֑ין וּ֝בְמַלְאָכָ֗יו יָשִׂ֥ים תָּהֳלָֽה׃

lines.text: Behold, he puts no trust in his servants. He charges his angels with error.
Lo, in His servants He putteth no credence, Nor in His messengers setteth praise.'

4.he: אַ֤ף ׀ שֹׁכְנֵ֬י בָֽתֵּי־חֹ֗מֶר אֲשֶׁר־בֶּעָפָ֥ר יְסוֹדָ֑ם יְ֝דַכְּא֗וּם לִפְנֵי־עָֽשׁ׃

lines.text: How much more, those who dwell in houses of clay, whose foundation is in the dust, who are crushed before the moth!
Also — the inhabitants of houses of clay, (Whose foundation [is] in the dust, They bruise them before a moth.)

4.he: מִבֹּ֣קֶר לָעֶ֣רֶב יֻכַּ֑תּוּ מִבְּלִ֥י מֵ֝שִׂ֗ים לָנֶ֥צַח יֹאבֵֽדוּ׃

lines.text: Between morning and evening they are destroyed. They perish forever without any regarding it.
From morning to evening are beaten down, Without any regarding, for ever they perish.

4.he: הֲלֹא־נִסַּ֣ע יִתְרָ֣ם בָּ֑ם יָ֝מ֗וּתוּ וְלֹ֣א בְחָכְמָֽה׃

lines.text: Isn’t their tent cord plucked up within them? They die, and that without wisdom.’
Hath not their excellency been removed with them? They die, and not in wisdom!

5.he: קְֽרָא־נָ֭א הֲיֵ֣שׁ עוֹנֶ֑ךָּ וְאֶל־מִ֖י מִקְּדֹשִׁ֣ים תִּפְנֶֽה׃

lines.text: “Call now; is there any who will answer you? To which of the holy ones will you turn?
Pray, call, is there any to answer thee? And unto which of the holy ones dost thou turn?

5.he: כִּֽי־לֶֽ֭אֱוִיל יַהֲרָג־כָּ֑עַשׂ וּ֝פֹתֶ֗ה תָּמִ֥ית קִנְאָֽה׃

lines.text: For resentment kills the foolish man, and jealousy kills the simple.
For provocation slayeth the perverse, And envy putteth to death the simple,

5.he: אֲֽנִי־רָ֭אִיתִי אֱוִ֣יל מַשְׁרִ֑ישׁ וָאֶקּ֖וֹב נָוֵ֣הוּ פִתְאֹֽם׃

lines.text: I have seen the foolish taking root, but suddenly I cursed his habitation.
I — I have seen the perverse taking root, And I mark his habitation straightway,

5.he: יִרְחֲק֣וּ בָנָ֣יו מִיֶּ֑שַׁע וְיִֽדַּכְּא֥וּ בַ֝שַּׁ֗עַר וְאֵ֣ין מַצִּֽיל׃

lines.text: His children are far from safety. They are crushed in the gate. Neither is there any to deliver them,
Far are his sons from safety, And they are bruised in the gate, And there is no deliverer.

5.he: אֲשֶׁ֤ר קְצִיר֨וֹ ׀ רָ֘עֵ֤ב יֹאכֵ֗ל וְאֶֽל־מִצִנִּ֥ים יִקָּחֵ֑הוּ וְשָׁאַ֖ף צַמִּ֣ים חֵילָֽם׃

lines.text: whose harvest the hungry eats up, and take it even out of the thorns. The snare gapes for their substance.
Whose harvest the hungry doth eat, And even from the thorns taketh it, And the designing swallowed their wealth.

5.he: כִּ֤י ׀ לֹא־יֵצֵ֣א מֵעָפָ֣ר אָ֑וֶן וּ֝מֵאֲדָמָ֗ה לֹא־יִצְמַ֥ח עָמָֽל׃

lines.text: For affliction doesn’t come out of the dust, neither does trouble spring out of the ground;
For sorrow cometh not forth from the dust, Nor from the ground springeth up misery.

5.he: כִּֽי־אָ֭דָם לְעָמָ֣ל יוּלָּ֑ד וּבְנֵי־רֶ֝֗שֶׁף יַגְבִּ֥יהוּ עֽוּף׃

lines.text: but man is born to trouble, as the sparks fly upward.
For man to misery is born, And the sparks go high to fly.

5.he: אוּלָ֗ם אֲ֭נִי אֶדְרֹ֣שׁ אֶל־אֵ֑ל וְאֶל־אֱ֝לֹהִ֗ים אָשִׂ֥ים דִּבְרָתִֽי׃

lines.text: “But as for me, I would seek God. I would commit my cause to God,
Yet I — I inquire for God, And for God I give my word,

5.he: עֹשֶׂ֣ה גְ֭דֹלוֹת וְאֵ֣ין חֵ֑קֶר נִ֝פְלָא֗וֹת עַד־אֵ֥ין מִסְפָּֽר׃

lines.text: who does great things that can’t be fathomed, marvelous things without number;
Doing great things, and there is no searching. Wonderful, till there is no numbering.

5.he: הַנֹּתֵ֣ן מָ֭טָר עַל־פְּנֵי־אָ֑רֶץ וְשֹׁ֥לֵֽחַ מַ֝יִם עַל־פְּנֵ֥י חוּצֽוֹת׃

lines.text: who gives rain on the earth, and sends waters on the fields;
Who is giving rain on the face of the land, And is sending waters on the out-places.

5.he: לָשׂ֣וּם שְׁפָלִ֣ים לְמָר֑וֹם וְ֝קֹדְרִ֗ים שָׂ֣גְבוּ יֶֽשַׁע׃

lines.text: so that he sets up on high those who are low, those who mourn are exalted to safety.
To set the low on a high place, And the mourners have been high [in] safety.

5.he: מֵ֭פֵר מַחְשְׁב֣וֹת עֲרוּמִ֑ים וְֽלֹא־תַעֲשֶׂ֥ינָה יְ֝דֵיהֶ֗ם תּוּשִׁיָּֽה׃

lines.text: He frustrates the plans of the crafty, So that their hands can’t perform their enterprise.
Making void thoughts of the subtile, And their hands do not execute wisdom.

5.he: לֹכֵ֣ד חֲכָמִ֣ים בְּעָרְמָ֑ם וַעֲצַ֖ת נִפְתָּלִ֣ים נִמְהָֽרָה׃

lines.text: He takes the wise in their own craftiness; the counsel of the cunning is carried headlong.
Capturing the wise in their subtilty, And the counsel of wrestling ones was hastened,

5.he: יוֹמָ֥ם יְפַגְּשׁוּ־חֹ֑שֶׁךְ וְ֝כַלַּ֗יְלָה יְֽמַשְׁשׁ֥וּ בַֽצָּהֳרָֽיִם׃

lines.text: They meet with darkness in the day time, and grope at noonday as in the night.
By day they meet darkness, And as night — they grope at noon.

5.he: וַיֹּ֣שַׁע מֵ֭חֶרֶב מִפִּיהֶ֑ם וּמִיַּ֖ד חָזָ֣ק אֶבְיֽוֹן׃

lines.text: But he saves from the sword of their mouth, even the needy from the hand of the mighty.
And He saveth the wasted from their mouth, And from a strong hand the needy,

5.he: וַתְּהִ֣י לַדַּ֣ל תִּקְוָ֑ה וְ֝עֹלָ֗תָה קָ֣פְצָה פִּֽיהָ׃

lines.text: So the poor has hope, and injustice shuts her mouth.
And there is hope to the poor, And perverseness hath shut her mouth.

5.he: הִנֵּ֤ה אַשְׁרֵ֣י אֱ֭נוֹשׁ יוֹכִחֶ֣נּֽוּ אֱל֑וֹהַּ וּמוּסַ֥ר שַׁ֝דַּ֗י אַל־תִּמְאָֽס׃

lines.text: “Behold, happy is the man whom God corrects. Therefore do not despise the chastening of the Almighty.
Lo, the happiness of mortal man, God doth reprove him: And the chastisement of the Mighty despise not,

5.he: כִּ֤י ה֣וּא יַכְאִ֣יב וְיֶחְבָּ֑שׁ יִ֝מְחַ֗ץ וידו תִּרְפֶּֽינָה׃

lines.text: For he wounds and binds up. He injures and his hands make whole.
For He doth pain, and He bindeth up, He smiteth, and His hands heal.

5.he: בְּשֵׁ֣שׁ צָ֭רוֹת יַצִּילֶ֑ךָּ וּבְשֶׁ֓בַע ׀ לֹא־יִגַּ֖ע בְּךָ֣ רָֽע׃

lines.text: He will deliver you in six troubles; yes, in seven no evil will touch you.
In six distresses He delivereth thee, And in seven evil striketh not on thee.

5.he: בְּ֭רָעָב פָּֽדְךָ֣ מִמָּ֑וֶת וּ֝בְמִלְחָמָ֗ה מִ֣ידֵי חָֽרֶב׃

lines.text: In famine he will redeem you from death; in war, from the power of the sword.
In famine He hath redeemed thee from death, And in battle from the hands of the sword.

5.he: בְּשׁ֣וֹט לָ֭שׁוֹן תֵּחָבֵ֑א וְֽלֹא־תִירָ֥א מִ֝שֹּׁ֗ד כִּ֣י יָבֽוֹא׃

lines.text: You will be hidden from the scourge of the tongue, neither will you be afraid of destruction when it comes.
When the tongue scourgeth thou art hid, And thou art not afraid of destruction, When it cometh.

5.he: לְשֹׁ֣ד וּלְכָפָ֣ן תִּשְׂחָ֑ק וּֽמֵחַיַּ֥ת הָ֝אָ֗רֶץ אַל־תִּירָֽא׃

lines.text: You will laugh at destruction and famine, neither will you be afraid of the animals of the earth.
At destruction and at hunger thou mockest, And of the beast of the earth, Thou art not afraid.

5.he: כִּ֤י עִם־אַבְנֵ֣י הַשָּׂדֶ֣ה בְרִיתֶ֑ךָ וְחַיַּ֥ת הַ֝שָּׂדֶ֗ה הָשְׁלְמָה־לָֽךְ׃

lines.text: For you will be allied with the stones of the field. The animals of the field will be at peace with you.
(For with sons of the field [is] thy covenant, And the beast of the field Hath been at peace with thee.)

5.he: וְֽ֭יָדַעְתָּ כִּי־שָׁל֣וֹם אָהֳלֶ֑ךָ וּֽפָקַדְתָּ֥ נָ֝וְךָ וְלֹ֣א תֶחֱטָֽא׃

lines.text: You will know that your tent is in peace. You will visit your fold, and will miss nothing.
And thou hast known that thy tent [is] peace, And inspected thy habitation, and errest not,

5.he: וְֽ֭יָדַעְתָּ כִּי־רַ֣ב זַרְעֶ֑ךָ וְ֝צֶאֱצָאֶ֗יךָ כְּעֵ֣שֶׂב הָאָֽרֶץ׃

lines.text: You will know also that your offspring will be great, Your offspring as the grass of the earth.
And hast known that numerous [is] Thy seed, And thine offspring as the herb of the earth;

5.he: תָּב֣וֹא בְכֶ֣לַח אֱלֵי־קָ֑בֶר כַּעֲל֖וֹת גָּדִ֣ישׁ בְּעִתּֽוֹ׃

lines.text: You will come to your grave in a full age, like a shock of grain comes in its season.
Thou comest in full age unto the grave, As the going up of a stalk in its season.

5.he: הִנֵּה־זֹ֭את חֲקַרְנ֥וּהָ כֶּֽן־הִ֑יא שְׁ֝מָעֶ֗נָּה וְאַתָּ֥ה דַֽע־לָֽךְ׃

lines.text: Look at this. We have searched it. It is so. Hear it, and know it for your good.”
Lo, this — we searched it out — it [is] right, hearken; And thou, know for thyself!

6.he: וַיַּ֥עַן אִיּ֗וֹב וַיֹּאמַֽר׃

lines.text: Then Job answered,
And Job answereth and saith: —

6.he: ל֗וּ שָׁק֣וֹל יִשָּׁקֵ֣ל כַּעְשִׂ֑י והיתי בְּֽמֹאזְנַ֥יִם יִשְׂאוּ־יָֽחַד׃

lines.text: “Oh that my anguish were weighed, and all my calamity laid in the balances!
O that my provocation were thoroughly weighed, And my calamity in balances They would lift up together!

6.he: כִּֽי־עַתָּ֗ה מֵח֣וֹל יַמִּ֣ים יִכְבָּ֑ד עַל־כֵּ֝֗ן דְּבָרַ֥י לָֽעוּ׃

lines.text: For now it would be heavier than the sand of the seas, therefore have my words been rash.
For now, than the sands of the sea it is heavier, Therefore my words have been rash.

6.he: כִּ֤י חִצֵּ֪י שַׁדַּ֡י עִמָּדִ֗י אֲשֶׁ֣ר חֲ֭מָתָם שֹׁתָ֣ה רוּחִ֑י בִּעוּתֵ֖י אֱל֣וֹהַּ יַֽעַרְכֽוּנִי׃

lines.text: For the arrows of the Almighty are within me. My spirit drinks up their poison. The terrors of God set themselves in array against me.
For arrows of the Mighty [are] with me, Whose poison is drinking up my spirit. Terrors of God array themselves [for] me!

6.he: הֲיִֽנְהַק־פֶּ֥רֶא עֲלֵי־דֶ֑שֶׁא אִ֥ם יִגְעֶה־שּׁ֝֗וֹר עַל־בְּלִילֽוֹ׃

lines.text: Does the wild donkey bray when he has grass? Or does the ox low over his fodder?
Brayeth a wild ass over tender grass? Loweth an ox over his provender?

6.he: הֲיֵאָכֵ֣ל תָּ֭פֵל מִבְּלִי־מֶ֑לַח אִם־יֶשׁ־טַ֝֗עַם בְּרִ֣יר חַלָּמֽוּת׃

lines.text: Can that which has no flavor be eaten without salt? Or is there any taste in the white of an egg?
Eaten is an insipid thing without salt? Is there sense in the drivel of dreams?

6.he: מֵאֲנָ֣ה לִנְגּ֣וֹעַ נַפְשִׁ֑י הֵ֝֗מָּה כִּדְוֵ֥י לַחְמִֽי׃

lines.text: My soul refuses to touch them. They are as loathsome food to me.
My soul is refusing to touch! They [are] as my sickening food.

6.he: מִֽי־יִ֭תֵּן תָּב֣וֹא שֶֽׁאֱלָתִ֑י וְ֝תִקְוָתִ֗י יִתֵּ֥ן אֱלֽוֹהַּ׃

lines.text: “Oh that I might have my request, that God would grant the thing that I long for,
O that my request may come, That God may grant my hope!

6.he: וְיֹאֵ֣ל אֱ֭לוֹהַּ וִֽידַכְּאֵ֑נִי יַתֵּ֥ר יָ֝ד֗וֹ וִֽיבַצְּעֵֽנִי׃

lines.text: even that it would please God to crush me; that he would let loose his hand, and cut me off!
That God would please — and bruise me, Loose His hand and cut me off!

6.he: וּ֥תְהִי ע֨וֹד ׀ נֶ֘חָ֤מָתִ֗י וַאֲסַלְּדָ֣ה בְ֭חִילָה לֹ֣א יַחְמ֑וֹל כִּי־לֹ֥א כִ֝חַ֗דְתִּי אִמְרֵ֥י קָדֽוֹשׁ׃

lines.text: Let still be my consolation, yes, let me exult in pain that doesn’t spare, that I have not denied the words of the Holy One.
And yet it is my comfort, (And I exult in pain — He doth not spare,) That I have not hidden The sayings of the Holy One.

6.he: מַה־כֹּחִ֥י כִֽי־אֲיַחֵ֑ל וּמַה־קִּ֝צִּ֗י כִּֽי־אַאֲרִ֥יךְ נַפְשִֽׁי׃

lines.text: What is my strength, that I should wait? What is my end, that I should be patient?
What [is] my power that I should hope? And what mine end That I should prolong my life?

6.he: אִם־כֹּ֣חַ אֲבָנִ֣ים כֹּחִ֑י אִֽם־בְּשָׂרִ֥י נָחֽוּשׁ׃

lines.text: Is my strength the strength of stones? Or is my flesh of bronze?
Is my strength the strength of stones? Is my flesh brazen?

6.he: הַאִ֬ם אֵ֣ין עֶזְרָתִ֣י בִ֑י וְ֝תֻשִׁיָּ֗ה נִדְּחָ֥ה מִמֶּֽנִּי׃

lines.text: Isn’t it that I have no help in me, That wisdom is driven quite from me?
Is not my help with me, And substance driven from me?

6.he: לַמָּ֣ס מֵרֵעֵ֣הוּ חָ֑סֶד וְיִרְאַ֖ת שַׁדַּ֣י יַעֲזֽוֹב׃

lines.text: “To him who is ready to faint, kindness should be shown from his friend; even to him who forsakes the fear of the Almighty.
To a despiser of his friends [is] shame, And the fear of the Mighty he forsaketh.

6.he: אַ֭חַי בָּגְד֣וּ כְמוֹ־נָ֑חַל כַּאֲפִ֖יק נְחָלִ֣ים יַעֲבֹֽרוּ׃

lines.text: My brothers have dealt deceitfully as a brook, as the channel of brooks that pass away;
My brethren have deceived as a brook, As a stream of brooks they pass away.

6.he: הַקֹּדְרִ֥ים מִנִּי־קָ֑רַח עָ֝לֵ֗ימוֹ יִתְעַלֶּם־שָֽׁלֶג׃

lines.text: Which are black by reason of the ice, in which the snow hides itself.
That are black because of ice, By them doth snow hide itself.

6.he: בְּ֭עֵת יְזֹרְב֣וּ נִצְמָ֑תוּ בְּ֝חֻמּ֗וֹ נִדְעֲכ֥וּ מִמְּקוֹמָֽם׃

lines.text: In the dry season, they vanish. When it is hot, they are consumed out of their place.
By the time they are warm they have been cut off, By its being hot they have been Extinguished from their place.

6.he: יִ֭לָּ֣פְתוּ אָרְח֣וֹת דַּרְכָּ֑ם יַעֲל֖וּ בַתֹּ֣הוּ וְיֹאבֵֽדוּ׃

lines.text: The caravans that travel beside them turn away. They go up into the waste, and perish.
Turn aside do the paths of their way, They ascend into emptiness, and are lost.

6.he: הִ֭בִּיטוּ אָרְח֣וֹת תֵּמָ֑א הֲלִיכֹ֥ת שְׁ֝בָ֗א קִוּוּ־לָֽמוֹ׃

lines.text: The caravans of Tema looked. The companies of Sheba waited for them.
Passengers of Tema looked expectingly, Travellers of Sheba hoped for them.

6.he: בֹּ֥שׁוּ כִּֽי־בָטָ֑ח בָּ֥אוּ עָ֝דֶ֗יהָ וַיֶּחְפָּֽרוּ׃

lines.text: They were distressed because they were confident. They came there, and were confounded.
They were ashamed that one hath trusted, They have come unto it and are confounded.

6.he: כִּֽי־עַ֭תָּה הֱיִ֣יתֶם לא תִּֽרְא֥וּ חֲ֝תַ֗ת וַתִּירָֽאוּ׃

lines.text: For now you are nothing. You see a terror, and are afraid.
Surely now ye have become the same! Ye see a downfall, and are afraid.

6.he: הֲֽכִי־אָ֭מַרְתִּי הָ֣בוּ לִ֑י וּ֝מִכֹּחֲכֶ֗ם שִׁחֲד֥וּ בַעֲדִֽי׃

lines.text: Did I say, ‘Give to me?’ or, ‘Offer a present for me from your substance?’
Is it because I said, Give to me? And, By your power bribe for me?

6.he: וּמַלְּט֥וּנִי מִיַּד־צָ֑ר וּמִיַּ֖ד עָרִיצִ֣ים תִּפְדּֽוּנִי׃

lines.text: or, ‘Deliver me from the adversary’s hand?’ or, ‘Redeem me from the hand of the oppressors?’
And, Deliver me from the hand of an adversary? And, From the hand of terrible ones ransom me?

6.he: ה֭וֹרוּנִי וַאֲנִ֣י אַחֲרִ֑ישׁ וּמַה־שָּׁ֝גִ֗יתִי הָבִ֥ינוּ לִֽי׃

lines.text: “Teach me, and I will hold my peace. Cause me to understand my error.
Shew me, and I — I keep silent, And what I have erred, let me understand.

6.he: מַה־נִּמְרְצ֥וּ אִמְרֵי־יֹ֑שֶׁר וּמַה־יּוֹכִ֖יחַ הוֹכֵ֣חַ מִכֶּֽם׃

lines.text: How forcible are words of uprightness! But your reproof, what does it reprove?
How powerful have been upright sayings, And what doth reproof from you reprove?

6.he: הַלְהוֹכַ֣ח מִלִּ֣ים תַּחְשֹׁ֑בוּ וּ֝לְר֗וּחַ אִמְרֵ֥י נֹאָֽשׁ׃

lines.text: Do you intend to reprove words, since the speeches of one who is desperate are as wind?
For reproof — do you reckon words? And for wind — sayings of the desperate.

6.he: אַף־עַל־יָת֥וֹם תַּפִּ֑ילוּ וְ֝תִכְר֗וּ עַל־רֵֽיעֲכֶֽם׃

lines.text: Yes, you would even cast lots for the fatherless, and make merchandise of your friend.
Anger on the fatherless ye cause to fall, And are strange to your friend.

6.he: וְ֭עַתָּה הוֹאִ֣ילוּ פְנוּ־בִ֑י וְעַל־פְּ֝נֵיכֶ֗ם אִם־אֲכַזֵּֽב׃

lines.text: Now therefore be pleased to look at me, for surely I will not lie to your face.
And, now, please, look upon me, Even to your face do I lie?

6.he: שֻֽׁבוּ־נָ֭א אַל־תְּהִ֣י עַוְלָ֑ה ושבי ע֝וֹד צִדְקִי־בָֽהּ׃

lines.text: Please return. Let there be no injustice. Yes, return again. My cause is righteous.
Turn back, I pray you, let it not be perverseness, Yea, turn back again — my righteousness [is] in it.

6.he: הֲיֵשׁ־בִּלְשׁוֹנִ֥י עַוְלָ֑ה אִם־חִ֝כִּ֗י לֹא־יָבִ֥ין הַוּֽוֹת׃

lines.text: Is there injustice on my tongue? Can’t my taste discern mischievous things?
Is there in my tongue perverseness? Discerneth not my palate desirable things?

7.he: הֲלֹא־צָבָ֣א לֶאֱנ֣וֹשׁ על־אָ֑רֶץ וְכִימֵ֖י שָׂכִ֣יר יָמָֽיו׃

lines.text: “Isn’t a man forced to labor on earth? Aren’t his days like the days of a hired hand?
Is there not a warfare to man on earth? And as the days of an hireling his days?

7.he: כְּעֶ֥בֶד יִשְׁאַף־צֵ֑ל וּ֝כְשָׂכִ֗יר יְקַוֶּ֥ה פָעֳלֽוֹ׃

lines.text: As a servant who earnestly desires the shadow, as a hireling who looks for his wages,
As a servant desireth the shadow, And as a hireling expecteth his wage,

7.he: כֵּ֤ן הָנְחַ֣לְתִּי לִ֭י יַרְחֵי־שָׁ֑וְא וְלֵיל֥וֹת עָ֝מָ֗ל מִנּוּ־לִֽי׃

lines.text: so am I made to possess months of misery, wearisome nights are appointed to me.
So I have been caused to inherit months of vanity, And nights of misery they numbered to me.

7.he: אִם־שָׁכַ֗בְתִּי וְאָמַ֗רְתִּי מָתַ֣י אָ֭קוּם וּמִדַּד־עָ֑רֶב וְשָׂבַ֖עְתִּי נְדֻדִ֣ים עֲדֵי־נָֽשֶׁף׃

lines.text: When I lie down, I say, ‘When will I arise, and the night be gone?’ I toss and turn until the dawning of the day.
If I lay down then I said, 'When do I rise!' And evening hath been measured, And I have been full of tossings till dawn.

7.he: לָ֘בַ֤שׁ בְּשָׂרִ֣י רִ֭מָּה וגיש עָפָ֑ר עוֹרִ֥י רָ֝גַ֗ע וַיִּמָּאֵֽס׃

lines.text: My flesh is clothed with worms and clods of dust. My skin closes up, and breaks out afresh.
Clothed hath been my flesh [with] worms, And a clod of dust, My skin hath been shrivelled and is loathsome,

7.he: יָמַ֣י קַ֭לּוּ מִנִּי־אָ֑רֶג וַ֝יִּכְל֗וּ בְּאֶ֣פֶס תִּקְוָֽה׃

lines.text: My days are swifter than a weaver’s shuttle, and are spent without hope.
My days swifter than a weaving machine, And they are consumed without hope.

7.he: זְ֭כֹר כִּי־ר֣וּחַ חַיָּ֑י לֹא־תָשׁ֥וּב עֵ֝ינִ֗י לִרְא֥וֹת טֽוֹב׃

lines.text: Oh remember that my life is a breath. My eye will no more see good.
Remember Thou that my life [is] a breath, Mine eye turneth not back to see good.

7.he: לֹֽא־תְ֭שׁוּרֵנִי עֵ֣ין רֹ֑אִי עֵינֶ֖יךָ בִּ֣י וְאֵינֶֽנִּי׃

lines.text: The eye of him who sees me will see me no more. Your eyes will be on me, but I will not be.
The eye of my beholder beholdeth me not. Thine eyes [are] upon me — and I am not.

7.he: כָּלָ֣ה עָ֭נָן וַיֵּלַ֑ךְ כֵּ֥ן יוֹרֵ֥ד שְׁ֝א֗וֹל לֹ֣א יַעֲלֶֽה׃

lines.text: As the cloud is consumed and vanishes away, so he who goes down to Sheol will come up no more.
Consumed hath been a cloud, and it goeth, So he who is going down to Sheol cometh not up.

7.he: לֹא־יָשׁ֣וּב ע֣וֹד לְבֵית֑וֹ וְלֹא־יַכִּירֶ֖נּוּ ע֣וֹד מְקֹמֽוֹ׃

lines.text: He will return no more to his house, neither will his place know him any more.
He turneth not again to his house, Nor doth his place discern him again.

7.he: גַּם־אֲנִי֮ לֹ֤א אֶחֱשָׂ֫ךְ פִּ֥י אֲֽ֭דַבְּרָה בְּצַ֣ר רוּחִ֑י אָ֝שִׂ֗יחָה בְּמַ֣ר נַפְשִֽׁי׃

lines.text: “Therefore I will not keep silent. I will speak in the anguish of my spirit. I will complain in the bitterness of my soul.
Also I — I withhold not my mouth — I speak in the distress of my spirit, I talk in the bitterness of my soul.

7.he: הֲֽיָם־אָ֭נִי אִם־תַּנִּ֑ין כִּֽי־תָשִׂ֖ים עָלַ֣י מִשְׁמָֽר׃

lines.text: Am I a sea, or a sea monster, that you put a guard over me?
A sea -[monster] am I, or a dragon, That thou settest over me a guard?

7.he: כִּֽי־אָ֭מַרְתִּי תְּנַחֲמֵ֣נִי עַרְשִׂ֑י יִשָּׂ֥א בְ֝שִׂיחִ֗י מִשְׁכָּבִֽי׃

lines.text: When I say, ‘My bed will comfort me. My couch will ease my complaint;’
When I said, 'My bed doth comfort me,' He taketh away in my talking my couch.

7.he: וְחִתַּתַּ֥נִי בַחֲלֹמ֑וֹת וּֽמֵחֶזְיֹנ֥וֹת תְּבַעֲתַֽנִּי׃

lines.text: then you scare me with dreams, and terrify me through visions:
And thou hast affrighted me with dreams, And from visions thou terrifiest me,

7.he: וַתִּבְחַ֣ר מַחֲנָ֣ק נַפְשִׁ֑י מָ֝֗וֶת מֵֽעַצְמוֹתָֽי׃

lines.text: so that my soul chooses strangling, death rather than my bones.
And my soul chooseth strangling, Death rather than my bones.

7.he: מָ֭אַסְתִּי לֹא־לְעֹלָ֣ם אֶֽחְיֶ֑ה חֲדַ֥ל מִ֝מֶּ֗נִּי כִּי־הֶ֥בֶל יָמָֽי׃

lines.text: I loathe my life. I don’t want to live forever. Leave me alone, for my days are but a breath.
I have wasted away — not to the age do I live. Cease from me, for my days [are] vanity.

7.he: מָֽה־אֱ֭נוֹשׁ כִּ֣י תְגַדְּלֶ֑נּוּ וְכִי־תָשִׁ֖ית אֵלָ֣יו לִבֶּֽךָ׃

lines.text: What is man, that you should magnify him, that you should set your mind on him,
What [is] man that Thou dost magnify him? And that Thou settest unto him Thy heart?

7.he: וַתִּפְקְדֶ֥נּוּ לִבְקָרִ֑ים לִ֝רְגָעִ֗ים תִּבְחָנֶֽנּוּ׃

lines.text: that you should visit him every morning, and test him every moment?
And inspectest him in the mornings, In the evenings dost try him?

7.he: כַּ֭מָּה לֹא־תִשְׁעֶ֣ה מִמֶּ֑נִּי לֹֽא־תַ֝רְפֵּ֗נִי עַד־בִּלְעִ֥י רֻקִּֽי׃

lines.text: How long will you not look away from me, nor leave me alone until I swallow down my spittle?
How long dost Thou not look from me? Thou dost not desist till I swallow my spittle.

7.he: חָטָ֡אתִי מָ֤ה אֶפְעַ֨ל ׀ לָךְ֮ נֹצֵ֪ר הָאָ֫דָ֥ם לָ֤מָה שַׂמְתַּ֣נִי לְמִפְגָּ֣ע לָ֑ךְ וָאֶהְיֶ֖ה עָלַ֣י לְמַשָּֽׂא׃

lines.text: If I have sinned, what do I do to you, you watcher of men? Why have you set me as a mark for you, so that I am a burden to myself?
I have sinned, what do I to Thee, O watcher of man? Why hast Thou set me for a mark to Thee, And I am for a burden to myself — and what?

7.he: וּמֶ֤ה ׀ לֹא־תִשָּׂ֣א פִשְׁעִי֮ וְתַעֲבִ֪יר אֶת־עֲוֺ֫נִ֥י כִּֽי־עַ֭תָּה לֶעָפָ֣ר אֶשְׁכָּ֑ב וְשִׁ֖חֲרְתַּ֣נִי וְאֵינֶֽנִּי׃

lines.text: Why do you not pardon my disobedience, and take away my iniquity? For now will I lie down in the dust. You will seek me diligently, but I will not be.”
Thou dost not take away my transgression, And cause to pass away mine iniquity, Because now, for dust I lie down: And Thou hast sought me — and I am not!

8.he: וַ֭יַּעַן בִּלְדַּ֥ד הַשּׁוּחִ֗י וַיֹאמַֽר׃

lines.text: Then Bildad the Shuhite answered,
And Bildad the Shuhite answereth and saith: —

8.he: עַד־אָ֥ן תְּמַלֶּל־אֵ֑לֶּה וְר֥וּחַ כַּ֝בִּיר אִמְרֵי־פִֽיךָ׃

lines.text: “How long will you speak these things? Shall the words of your mouth be a mighty wind?
Till when dost thou speak these things? And a strong wind — sayings of thy mouth?

8.he: הַ֭אֵל יְעַוֵּ֣ת מִשְׁפָּ֑ט וְאִם־שַׁ֝דַּ֗י יְעַוֵּֽת־צֶֽדֶק׃

lines.text: Does God pervert justice? Or does the Almighty pervert righteousness?
Doth God pervert judgment? And doth the Mighty One pervert justice?

8.he: אִם־בָּנֶ֥יךָ חָֽטְאוּ־ל֑וֹ וַֽ֝יְשַׁלְּחֵ֗ם בְּיַד־פִּשְׁעָֽם׃

lines.text: If your children have sinned against him, he has delivered them into the hand of their disobedience.
If thy sons have sinned before Him, And He doth send them away, By the hand of their transgression,

8.he: אִם־אַ֭תָּה תְּשַׁחֵ֣ר אֶל־אֵ֑ל וְאֶל־שַׁ֝דַּ֗י תִּתְחַנָּֽן׃

lines.text: If you want to seek God diligently, make your supplication to the Almighty.
If thou dost seek early unto God, And unto the Mighty makest supplication,

8.he: אִם־זַ֥ךְ וְיָשָׁ֗ר אָ֥תָּה כִּי־עַ֭תָּה יָעִ֣יר עָלֶ֑יךָ וְ֝שִׁלַּ֗ם נְוַ֣ת צִדְקֶֽךָ׃

lines.text: If you were pure and upright, surely now he would awaken for you, and make the habitation of your righteousness prosperous.
If pure and upright thou [art], Surely now He waketh for thee, And hath completed The habitation of thy righteousness.

8.he: וְהָיָ֣ה רֵאשִׁיתְךָ֣ מִצְעָ֑ר וְּ֝אַחֲרִיתְךָ֗ יִשְׂגֶּ֥ה מְאֹֽד׃

lines.text: Though your beginning was small, yet your latter end would greatly increase.
And thy beginning hath been small, And thy latter end is very great.

8.he: כִּֽי־שְׁאַל־נָ֭א לְדֹ֣ר רִישׁ֑וֹן וְ֝כוֹנֵ֗ן לְחֵ֣קֶר אֲבוֹתָֽם׃

lines.text: “Please inquire of past generations. Find out about the learning of their fathers.
For, ask I pray thee of a former generation, And prepare to a search of their fathers,

8.he: כִּֽי־תְמ֣וֹל אֲ֭נַחְנוּ וְלֹ֣א נֵדָ֑ע כִּ֤י צֵ֖ל יָמֵ֣ינוּ עֲלֵי־אָֽרֶץ׃

lines.text: (For we are but of yesterday, and know nothing, because our days on earth are a shadow.)
(For of yesterday we [are], and we know not, For a shadow [are] our days on earth.)

8.he: הֲלֹא־הֵ֣ם י֭וֹרוּךָ יֹ֣אמְרוּ לָ֑ךְ וּ֝מִלִּבָּ֗ם יוֹצִ֥אוּ מִלִּֽים׃

lines.text: Shall they not teach you, tell you, and utter words out of their heart?
Do they not shew thee — speak to thee, And from their heart bring forth words?

8.he: הֲיִֽגְאֶה־גֹּ֭מֶא בְּלֹ֣א בִצָּ֑ה יִשְׂגֶּה־אָ֥חוּ בְלִי־מָֽיִם׃

lines.text: “Can the papyrus grow up without mire? Can the rushes grow without water?
'Doth a rush wise without mire? A reed increase without water?

8.he: עֹדֶ֣נּוּ בְ֭אִבּוֹ לֹ֣א יִקָּטֵ֑ף וְלִפְנֵ֖י כָל־חָצִ֣יר יִיבָֽשׁ׃

lines.text: While it is yet in its greenness, not cut down, it withers before any other reed.
While it [is] in its budding — uncropped, Even before any herb it withereth.

8.he: כֵּ֗ן אָ֭רְחוֹת כָּל־שֹׁ֣כְחֵי אֵ֑ל וְתִקְוַ֖ת חָנֵ֣ף תֹּאבֵֽד׃

lines.text: So are the paths of all who forget God. The hope of the godless man will perish,
So [are] the paths of all forgetting God, And the hope of the profane doth perish,

8.he: אֲשֶׁר־יָק֥וֹט כִּסְל֑וֹ וּבֵ֥ית עַ֝כָּבִ֗ישׁ מִבְטַחֽוֹ׃

lines.text: Whose confidence will break apart, Whose trust is a spider’s web.
Whose confidence is loathsome, And the house of a spider his trust.

8.he: יִשָּׁעֵ֣ן עַל־בֵּ֭יתוֹ וְלֹ֣א יַעֲמֹ֑ד יַחֲזִ֥יק בּ֝֗וֹ וְלֹ֣א יָקֽוּם׃

lines.text: He will lean on his house, but it will not stand. He will cling to it, but it will not endure.
He leaneth on his house — and it standeth not: He taketh hold on it — and it abideth not.

8.he: רָטֹ֣ב ה֭וּא לִפְנֵי־שָׁ֑מֶשׁ וְעַ֥ל גַּ֝נָּת֗וֹ יֹֽנַקְתּ֥וֹ תֵצֵֽא׃

lines.text: He is green before the sun. His shoots go out along his garden.
Green he [is] before the sun, And over his garden his branch goeth out.

8.he: עַל־גַּ֭ל שָֽׁרָשָׁ֣יו יְסֻבָּ֑כוּ בֵּ֖ית אֲבָנִ֣ים יֶחֱזֶֽה׃

lines.text: His roots are wrapped around the rock pile. He sees the place of stones.
By a heap his roots are wrapped, A house of stones he looketh for.

8.he: אִם־יְבַלְּעֶ֥נּוּ מִמְּקוֹמ֑וֹ וְכִ֥חֶשׁ בּ֝֗וֹ לֹ֣א רְאִיתִֽיךָ׃

lines.text: If he is destroyed from his place, then it will deny him, saying, ‘I have not seen you.’
If [one] doth destroy him from his place, Then it hath feigned concerning him, I have not seen thee!

8.he: הֶן־ה֭וּא מְשׂ֣וֹשׂ דַּרְכּ֑וֹ וּ֝מֵעָפָ֗ר אַחֵ֥ר יִצְמָֽחוּ׃

lines.text: Behold, this is the joy of his way: out of the earth, others will spring.
Lo, this [is] the joy of his way, And from the dust others spring up.'

8.he: הֶן־אֵ֭ל לֹ֣א יִמְאַס־תָּ֑ם וְלֹֽא־יַ֝חֲזִ֗יק בְּיַד־מְרֵעִֽים׃

lines.text: “Behold, God will not cast away a blameless man, neither will he uphold the evildoers.
Lo, God doth not reject the perfect, Nor taketh hold on the hand of evil doers.

8.he: עַד־יְמַלֵּ֣ה שְׂח֣וֹק פִּ֑יךָ וּשְׂפָתֶ֥יךָ תְרוּעָֽה׃

lines.text: He will still fill your mouth with laughter, your lips with shouting.
While he filleth with laughter thy mouth, And thy lips with shouting,

8.he: שֹׂנְאֶ֥יךָ יִלְבְּשׁוּ־בֹ֑שֶׁת וְאֹ֖הֶל רְשָׁעִ֣ים אֵינֶֽנּוּ׃

lines.text: Those who hate you will be clothed with shame. The tent of the wicked will be no more.”
Those hating thee do put on shame, And the tent of the wicked is not!

9.he: וַיַּ֥עַן אִיּ֗וֹב וַיֹּאמַֽר׃

lines.text: Then Job answered,
And Job answereth and saith: —

9.he: אָ֭מְנָם יָדַ֣עְתִּי כִי־כֵ֑ן וּמַה־יִּצְדַּ֖ק אֱנ֣וֹשׁ עִם־אֵֽל׃

lines.text: “Truly I know that it is so, but how can man be just with God?
Truly I have known that [it is] so, And what — is man righteous with God?

9.he: אִם־יַ֭חְפֹּץ לָרִ֣יב עִמּ֑וֹ לֹֽא־יַ֝עֲנֶ֗נּוּ אַחַ֥ת מִנִּי־אָֽלֶף׃

lines.text: If he is pleased to contend with him, he can’t answer him one time in a thousand.
If he delight to strive with Him — He doth not answer him one of a thousand.

9.he: חֲכַ֣ם לֵ֭בָב וְאַמִּ֣יץ כֹּ֑חַ מִֽי־הִקְשָׁ֥ה אֵ֝לָ֗יו וַיִּשְׁלָֽם׃

lines.text: God who is wise in heart, and mighty in strength: who has hardened himself against him and prospered?
Wise in heart and strong in power — Who hath hardened toward Him and is at peace?

9.he: הַמַּעְתִּ֣יק הָ֭רִים וְלֹ֣א יָדָ֑עוּ אֲשֶׁ֖ר הֲפָכָ֣ם בְּאַפּֽוֹ׃

lines.text: He removes the mountains, and they don’t know it, when he overturns them in his anger.
Who is removing mountains, And they have not known, Who hath overturned them in His anger.

9.he: הַמַּרְגִּ֣יז אֶ֭רֶץ מִמְּקוֹמָ֑הּ וְ֝עַמּוּדֶ֗יהָ יִתְפַלָּצֽוּן׃

lines.text: He shakes the earth out of its place. Its pillars tremble.
Who is shaking earth from its place, And its pillars move themselves.

9.he: הָאֹמֵ֣ר לַ֭חֶרֶס וְלֹ֣א יִזְרָ֑ח וּבְעַ֖ד כּוֹכָבִ֣ים יַחְתֹּֽם׃

lines.text: He commands the sun and it doesn’t rise, and seals up the stars.
Who is speaking to the sun, and it riseth not, And the stars He sealeth up.

9.he: נֹטֶ֣ה שָׁמַ֣יִם לְבַדּ֑וֹ וְ֝דוֹרֵ֗ךְ עַל־בָּ֥מֳתֵי יָֽם׃

lines.text: He alone stretches out the heavens, and treads on the waves of the sea.
Stretching out the heavens by Himself, And treading on the heights of the sea,

9.he: עֹֽשֶׂה־עָ֭שׁ כְּסִ֥יל וְכִימָ֗ה וְחַדְרֵ֥י תֵמָֽן׃

lines.text: He makes the Bear, Orion, and the Pleiades, and the rooms of the south.
Making Osh, Kesil, and Kimah, And the inner chambers of the south.

9.he: עֹשֶׂ֣ה גְ֭דֹלוֹת עַד־אֵ֣ין חֵ֑קֶר וְנִפְלָא֗וֹת עַד־אֵ֥ין מִסְפָּֽר׃

lines.text: He does great things past finding out; yes, marvelous things without number.
Doing great things till there is no searching, And wonderful, till there is no numbering.

9.he: הֵ֤ן יַעֲבֹ֣ר עָ֭לַי וְלֹ֣א אֶרְאֶ֑ה וְ֝יַחֲלֹ֗ף וְֽלֹא־אָבִ֥ין לֽוֹ׃

lines.text: Behold, he goes by me, and I don’t see him. He passes on also, but I don’t perceive him.
Lo, He goeth over by me, and I see not, And He passeth on, and I attend not to it.

9.he: הֵ֣ן יַ֭חְתֹּף מִ֣י יְשִׁיבֶ֑נּוּ מִֽי־יֹאמַ֥ר אֵ֝לָ֗יו מַֽה־תַּעֲשֶֽׂה׃

lines.text: Behold, he snatches away. Who can hinder him? Who will ask him, ‘What are you doing?’
Lo, He snatches away, who bringeth it back? Who saith unto Him, 'What dost Thou?'

9.he: אֱ֭לוֹהַּ לֹא־יָשִׁ֣יב אַפּ֑וֹ תחתו שָׁ֝חֲח֗וּ עֹ֣זְרֵי רָֽהַב׃

lines.text: “God will not withdraw his anger. The helpers of Rahab stoop under him.
God doth not turn back His anger, Under Him bowed have proud helpers.

9.he: אַ֭ף כִּֽי־אָנֹכִ֣י אֶֽעֱנֶ֑נּוּ אֶבְחֲרָ֖ה דְבָרַ֣י עִמּֽוֹ׃

lines.text: How much less will I answer him, And choose my words to argue with him?
How much less do I — I answer Him? Choose out my words with Him?

9.he: אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִם־צָ֭דַקְתִּי לֹ֣א אֶעֱנֶ֑ה לִ֝מְשֹׁפְטִ֗י אֶתְחַנָּֽן׃

lines.text: Though I were righteous, yet I wouldn’t answer him. I would make supplication to my judge.
Whom, though I were righteous, I answer not, For my judgment I make supplication.

9.he: אִם־קָרָ֥אתִי וַֽיַּעֲנֵ֑נִי לֹֽא־אַ֝אֲמִ֗ין כִּֽי־יַאֲזִ֥ין קוֹלִֽי׃

lines.text: If I had called, and he had answered me, yet I wouldn’t believe that he listened to my voice.
Though I had called and He answereth me, I do not believe that He giveth ear [to] my voice.

9.he: אֲשֶׁר־בִּשְׂעָרָ֥ה יְשׁוּפֵ֑נִי וְהִרְבָּ֖ה פְצָעַ֣י חִנָּֽם׃

lines.text: For he breaks me with a storm, and multiplies my wounds without cause.
Because with a tempest He bruiseth me, And hath multiplied my wounds for nought.

9.he: לֹֽא־יִ֭תְּנֵנִי הָשֵׁ֣ב רוּחִ֑י כִּ֥י יַ֝שְׂבִּעַ֗נִי מַמְּרֹרִֽים׃

lines.text: He will not allow me to catch my breath, but fills me with bitterness.
He permitteth me not to refresh my spirit, But filleth me with bitter things.

9.he: אִם־לְכֹ֣חַ אַמִּ֣יץ הִנֵּ֑ה וְאִם־לְ֝מִשְׁפָּ֗ט מִ֣י יוֹעִידֵֽנִי׃

lines.text: If it is a matter of strength, behold, he is mighty! If of justice, ‘Who,’ says he, ‘will summon me?’
If of power, lo, the Strong One; And if of judgment — who doth convene me?

9.he: אִם־אֶ֭צְדָּק פִּ֣י יַרְשִׁיעֵ֑נִי תָּֽם־אָ֝֗נִי וַֽיַּעְקְשֵֽׁנִי׃

lines.text: Though I am righteous, my own mouth will condemn me. Though I am blameless, it will prove me perverse.
If I be righteous, Mine mouth doth declare me wicked, Perfect I am! — it declareth me perverse.

9.he: תָּֽם־אָ֭נִי לֹֽא־אֵדַ֥ע נַפְשִׁ֗י אֶמְאַ֥ס חַיָּֽי׃

lines.text: I am blameless. I don’t respect myself. I despise my life.
Perfect I am! — I know not my soul, I despise my life.

9.he: אַחַ֗ת הִ֥יא עַל־כֵּ֥ן אָמַ֑רְתִּי תָּ֥ם וְ֝רָשָׁ֗ע ה֣וּא מְכַלֶּֽה׃

lines.text: “It is all the same. Therefore I say he destroys the blameless and the wicked.
It is the same thing, therefore I said, 'The perfect and the wicked He is consuming.'

9.he: אִם־שׁ֭וֹט יָמִ֣ית פִּתְאֹ֑ם לְמַסַּ֖ת נְקִיִּ֣ם יִלְעָֽג׃

lines.text: If the scourge kills suddenly, he will mock at the trial of the innocent.
If a scourge doth put to death suddenly, At the trial of the innocent He laugheth.

9.he: אֶ֤רֶץ ׀ נִתְּנָ֬ה בְֽיַד־רָשָׁ֗ע פְּנֵֽי־שֹׁפְטֶ֥יהָ יְכַסֶּ֑ה אִם־לֹ֖א אֵפ֣וֹא מִי־הֽוּא׃

lines.text: The earth is given into the hand of the wicked. He covers the faces of its judges. If not he, then who is it?
Earth hath been given Into the hand of the wicked one. The face of its judges he covereth, If not — where, who [is] he?

9.he: וְיָמַ֣י קַ֭לּוּ מִנִּי־רָ֑ץ בָּֽ֝רְח֗וּ לֹא־רָא֥וּ טוֹבָֽה׃

lines.text: “Now my days are swifter than a runner. They flee away. They see no good.
My days have been swifter than a runner, They have fled, they have not seen good,

9.he: חָ֭לְפוּ עִם־אֳנִיּ֣וֹת אֵבֶ֑ה כְּ֝נֶ֗שֶׁר יָט֥וּשׂ עֲלֵי־אֹֽכֶל׃

lines.text: They have passed away as the swift ships, as the eagle that swoops on the prey.
They have passed on with ships of reed, As an eagle darteth on food.

9.he: אִם־אָ֭מְרִי אֶשְׁכְּחָ֣ה שִׂיחִ֑י אֶעֶזְבָ֖ה פָנַ֣י וְאַבְלִֽיגָה׃

lines.text: If I say, ‘I will forget my complaint, I will put off my sad face, and cheer up;’
Though I say, 'I forget my talking, I forsake my corner, and I brighten up!'

9.he: יָגֹ֥רְתִּי כָל־עַצְּבֹתָ֑י יָ֝דַ֗עְתִּי כִּי־לֹ֥א תְנַקֵּֽנִי׃

lines.text: I am afraid of all my sorrows, I know that you will not hold me innocent.
I have been afraid of all my griefs, I have known that Thou dost not acquit me.

9.he: אָנֹכִ֥י אֶרְשָׁ֑ע לָמָּה־זֶּ֝֗ה הֶ֣בֶל אִיגָֽע׃

lines.text: I will be condemned. Why then do I labor in vain?
I — I am become wicked; why [is] this? [In] vain I labour.

9.he: אִם־הִתְרָחַ֥צְתִּי במו־שָׁ֑לֶג וַ֝הֲזִכּ֗וֹתִי בְּבֹ֣ר כַּפָּֽי׃

lines.text: If I wash myself with snow, and cleanse my hands with lye,
If I have washed myself with snow-water, And purified with soap my hands,

9.he: אָ֭ז בַּשַּׁ֣חַת תִּטְבְּלֵ֑נִי וְ֝תִֽעֲב֗וּנִי שַׂלְמוֹתָֽי׃

lines.text: yet you will plunge me in the ditch. My own clothes will abhor me.
Then in corruption Thou dost dip me, And my garments have abominated me.

9.he: כִּי־לֹא־אִ֣ישׁ כָּמֹ֣נִי אֶֽעֱנֶ֑נּוּ נָב֥וֹא יַ֝חְדָּ֗ו בַּמִּשְׁפָּֽט׃

lines.text: For he is not a man, as I am, that I should answer him, that we should come together in judgment.
But if a man like myself — I answer him, We come together into judgment.

9.he: לֹ֣א יֵשׁ־בֵּינֵ֣ינוּ מוֹכִ֑יחַ יָשֵׁ֖ת יָד֣וֹ עַל־שְׁנֵֽינוּ׃

lines.text: There is no umpire between us, that might lay his hand on us both.
If there were between us an umpire, He doth place his hand on us both.

9.he: יָסֵ֣ר מֵעָלַ֣י שִׁבְט֑וֹ וְ֝אֵמָת֗וֹ אַֽל־תְּבַעֲתַֽנִּי׃

lines.text: Let him take his rod away from me. Let his terror not make me afraid;
He doth turn aside from off me his rod, And His terror doth not make me afraid,

9.he: אַֽ֭דַבְּרָה וְלֹ֣א אִירָאֶ֑נּוּ כִּ֥י לֹא־כֵ֥ן אָ֝נֹכִ֗י עִמָּדִֽי׃

lines.text: then I would speak, and not fear him, for I am not so in myself.
I speak, and do not fear Him, But I am not right with myself.

10.he: נָֽקְטָ֥ה נַפְשִׁ֗י בְּחַ֫יָּ֥י אֶֽעֶזְבָ֣ה עָלַ֣י שִׂיחִ֑י אֲ֝דַבְּרָה֗ בְּמַ֣ר נַפְשִֽׁי׃

lines.text: “My soul is weary of my life. I will give free course to my complaint. I will speak in the bitterness of my soul.
My soul hath been weary of my life, I leave off my talking to myself, I speak in the bitterness of my soul.

10.he: אֹמַ֣ר אֶל־אֱ֭לוֹהַּ אַל־תַּרְשִׁיעֵ֑נִי הֽ֝וֹדִיעֵ֗נִי עַ֣ל מַה־תְּרִיבֵֽנִי׃

lines.text: I will tell God, ‘Do not condemn me. Show me why you contend with me.
I say unto God, 'Do not condemn me, Let me know why Thou dost strive [with] me.

10.he: הֲט֤וֹב לְךָ֨ ׀ כִּֽי־תַעֲשֹׁ֗ק כִּֽי־תִ֭מְאַס יְגִ֣יעַ כַּפֶּ֑יךָ וְעַל־עֲצַ֖ת רְשָׁעִ֣ים הוֹפָֽעְתָּ׃

lines.text: Is it good to you that you should oppress, that you should despise the work of your hands, and smile on the counsel of the wicked?
Is it good for Thee that Thou dost oppress? That Thou despisest the labour of Thy hands, And on the counsel of the wicked hast shone?

10.he: הַעֵינֵ֣י בָשָׂ֣ר לָ֑ךְ אִם־כִּרְא֖וֹת אֱנ֣וֹשׁ תִּרְאֶֽה׃

lines.text: Do you have eyes of flesh? Or do you see as man sees?
Eyes of flesh hast Thou? As man seeth — seest Thou?

10.he: הֲכִימֵ֣י אֱנ֣וֹשׁ יָמֶ֑יךָ אִם־שְׁ֝נוֹתֶ֗יךָ כִּ֣ימֵי גָֽבֶר׃

lines.text: Are your days as the days of mortals, or your years as man’s years,
As the days of man [are] Thy days? Thy years as the days of a man?

10.he: כִּֽי־תְבַקֵּ֥שׁ לַעֲוֺנִ֑י וּ֭לְחַטָּאתִ֥י תִדְרֽוֹשׁ׃

lines.text: that you inquire after my iniquity, and search after my sin?
That Thou inquirest for mine iniquity, And for my sin seekest?

10.he: עַֽל־דַּ֭עְתְּךָ כִּי־לֹ֣א אֶרְשָׁ֑ע וְאֵ֖ין מִיָּדְךָ֣ מַצִּֽיל׃

lines.text: Although you know that I am not wicked, there is no one who can deliver out of your hand.
For Thou knowest that I am not wicked, And there is no deliverer from Thy hand.

10.he: יָדֶ֣יךָ עִ֭צְּבוּנִי וַֽיַּעֲשׂ֑וּנִי יַ֥חַד סָ֝בִ֗יב וַֽתְּבַלְּעֵֽנִי׃

lines.text: “ ‘Your hands have framed me and fashioned me altogether, yet you destroy me.
Thy hands have taken pains about me, And they make me together round about, And Thou swallowest me up!

10.he: זְכָר־נָ֭א כִּי־כַחֹ֣מֶר עֲשִׂיתָ֑נִי וְֽאֶל־עָפָ֥ר תְּשִׁיבֵֽנִי׃

lines.text: Remember, I beg you, that you have fashioned me as clay. Will you bring me into dust again?
Remember, I pray Thee, That as clay Thou hast made me, And unto dust Thou dost bring me back.

10.he: הֲלֹ֣א כֶ֭חָלָב תַּתִּיכֵ֑נִי וְ֝כַגְּבִנָּ֗ה תַּקְפִּיאֵֽנִי׃

lines.text: Haven’t you poured me out like milk, and curdled me like cheese?
Dost Thou not as milk pour me out? And as cheese curdle me?

10.he: ע֣וֹר וּ֭בָשָׂר תַּלְבִּישֵׁ֑נִי וּֽבַעֲצָמ֥וֹת וְ֝גִידִ֗ים תְּסֹכְכֵֽנִי׃

lines.text: You have clothed me with skin and flesh, and knit me together with bones and sinews.
Skin and flesh Thou dost put on me, And with bones and sinews dost fence me.

10.he: חַיִּ֣ים וָ֭חֶסֶד עָשִׂ֣יתָ עִמָּדִ֑י וּ֝פְקֻדָּתְךָ֗ שָֽׁמְרָ֥ה רוּחִֽי׃

lines.text: You have granted me life and loving kindness. Your visitation has preserved my spirit.
Life and kindness Thou hast done with me. And Thy inspection hath preserved my spirit.

10.he: וְ֭אֵלֶּה צָפַ֣נְתָּ בִלְבָבֶ֑ךָ יָ֝דַ֗עְתִּי כִּי־זֹ֥את עִמָּֽךְ׃

lines.text: Yet you hid these things in your heart. I know that this is with you:
And these Thou hast laid up in Thy heart, I have known that this [is] with Thee.

10.he: אִם־חָטָ֥אתִי וּשְׁמַרְתָּ֑נִי וּ֝מֵעֲוֺנִ֗י לֹ֣א תְנַקֵּֽנִי׃

lines.text: if I sin, then you mark me. You will not acquit me from my iniquity.
If I sinned, then Thou hast observed me, And from mine iniquity dost not acquit me,

10.he: אִם־רָשַׁ֡עְתִּי אַלְלַ֬י לִ֗י וְ֭צָדַקְתִּי לֹא־אֶשָּׂ֣א רֹאשִׁ֑י שְׂבַ֥ע קָ֝ל֗וֹן וּרְאֵ֥ה עָנְיִֽי׃

lines.text: If I am wicked, woe to me. If I am righteous, I still will not lift up my head, being filled with disgrace, and conscious of my affliction.
If I have done wickedly — woe to me, And righteously — I lift not up my head, Full of shame — then see my affliction,

10.he: וְ֭יִגְאֶה כַּשַּׁ֣חַל תְּצוּדֵ֑נִי וְ֝תָשֹׁ֗ב תִּתְפַּלָּא־בִֽי׃

lines.text: If my head is held high, you hunt me like a lion. Again you show yourself powerful to me.
And it riseth — as a lion Thou huntest me. And Thou turnest back — Thou shewest Thyself wonderful in me.

10.he: תְּחַדֵּ֬שׁ עֵדֶ֨יךָ ׀ נֶגְדִּ֗י וְתֶ֣רֶב כַּֽ֭עַשְׂךָ עִמָּדִ֑י חֲלִיפ֖וֹת וְצָבָ֣א עִמִּֽי׃

lines.text: You renew your witnesses against me, and increase your indignation on me. Changes and warfare are with me.
Thou renewest Thy witnesses against me, And dost multiply Thine anger with me, Changes and warfare [are] with me.

10.he: וְלָ֣מָּה מֵ֭רֶחֶם הֹצֵאתָ֑נִי אֶ֝גְוַ֗ע וְעַ֣יִן לֹא־תִרְאֵֽנִי׃

lines.text: “ ‘Why, then, have you brought me out of the womb? I wish I had given up the spirit, and no eye had seen me.
And why from the womb Hast Thou brought me forth? I expire, and the eye doth not see me.

10.he: כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹא־הָיִ֣יתִי אֶהְיֶ֑ה מִ֝בֶּ֗טֶן לַקֶּ֥בֶר אוּבָֽל׃

lines.text: I should have been as though I had not been. I should have been carried from the womb to the grave.
As I had not been, I am, From the belly to the grave I am brought,

10.he: הֲלֹא־מְעַ֣ט יָמַ֣י יחדל ישית מִ֝מֶּ֗נִּי וְאַבְלִ֥יגָה מְּעָֽט׃

lines.text: Aren’t my days few? Stop! Leave me alone, that I may find a little comfort,
Are not my days few? Cease then, and put from me, And I brighten up a little,

10.he: בְּטֶ֣רֶם אֵ֭לֵךְ וְלֹ֣א אָשׁ֑וּב אֶל־אֶ֖רֶץ חֹ֣שֶׁךְ וְצַלְמָֽוֶת׃

lines.text: before I go where I will not return from, to the land of darkness and of the shadow of death;
Before I go, and return not, Unto a land of darkness and death-shade,

10.he: אֶ֤רֶץ עֵיפָ֨תָה ׀ כְּמ֥וֹ אֹ֗פֶל צַ֭לְמָוֶת וְלֹ֥א סְדָרִ֗ים וַתֹּ֥פַע כְּמוֹ־אֹֽפֶל׃

lines.text: the land dark as midnight, of the shadow of death, without any order, where the light is as midnight.’ ”
A land of obscurity as thick darkness, Death-shade — and no order, And the shining [is] as thick darkness.'

11.he: וַ֭יַּעַן צֹפַ֥ר הַֽנַּעֲמָתִ֗י וַיֹּאמַֽר׃

lines.text: Then Zophar, the Naamathite, answered,
And Zophar the Naamathite answereth and saith: —

11.he: הֲרֹ֣ב דְּ֭בָרִים לֹ֣א יֵעָנֶ֑ה וְאִם־אִ֖ישׁ שְׂפָתַ֣יִם יִצְדָּֽק׃

lines.text: “Shouldn’t the multitude of words be answered? Should a man full of talk be justified?
Is a multitude of words not answered? And is a man of lips justified?

11.he: בַּ֭דֶּיךָ מְתִ֣ים יַחֲרִ֑ישׁו וַ֝תִּלְעַ֗ג וְאֵ֣ין מַכְלִֽם׃

lines.text: Should your boastings make men hold their peace? When you mock, will no man make you ashamed?
Thy devices make men keep silent, Thou scornest, and none is causing blushing!

11.he: וַ֭תֹּאמֶר זַ֣ךְ לִקְחִ֑י וּ֝בַ֗ר הָיִ֥יתִי בְעֵינֶֽיךָ׃

lines.text: For you say, ‘My doctrine is pure. I am clean in your eyes.’
And thou sayest, 'Pure [is] my discourse, And clean I have been in Thine eyes.'

11.he: וְֽאוּלָ֗ם מִֽי־יִתֵּ֣ן אֱל֣וֹהַּ דַּבֵּ֑ר וְיִפְתַּ֖ח שְׂפָתָ֣יו עִמָּֽךְ׃

lines.text: But oh that God would speak, and open his lips against you,
And yet, O that God had spoken! And doth open His lips with thee.

11.he: וְיַגֶּד־לְךָ֨ ׀ תַּֽעֲלֻמ֣וֹת חָכְמָה֮ כִּֽי־כִפְלַ֪יִם לְֽת֫וּשִׁיָּ֥ה וְדַ֡ע כִּֽי־יַשֶּׁ֥ה לְךָ֥ אֱ֝ל֗וֹהַ מֵעֲוֺנֶֽךָ׃

lines.text: that he would show you the secrets of wisdom! For true wisdom has two sides. Know therefore that God exacts of you less than your iniquity deserves.
And declare to thee secrets of wisdom, For counsel hath foldings. And know thou that God forgetteth for thee, [Some] of thine iniquity.

11.he: הַחֵ֣קֶר אֱל֣וֹהַ תִּמְצָ֑א אִ֤ם עַד־תַּכְלִ֖ית שַׁדַּ֣י תִּמְצָֽא׃

lines.text: “Can you fathom the mystery of God? Or can you probe the limits of the Almighty?
By searching dost thou find out God? Unto perfection find out the Mighty One?

11.he: גָּבְהֵ֣י שָׁ֭מַיִם מַה־תִּפְעָ֑ל עֲמֻקָּ֥ה מִ֝שְּׁא֗וֹל מַה־תֵּדָֽע׃

lines.text: They are high as heaven. What can you do? They are deeper than Sheol. What can you know?
Heights of the heavens! — what dost thou? Deeper than Sheol! — what knowest thou?

11.he: אֲרֻכָּ֣ה מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִדָּ֑הּ וּ֝רְחָבָ֗ה מִנִּי־יָֽם׃

lines.text: Its measure is longer than the earth, and broader than the sea.
Longer than earth [is] its measure, And broader than the sea.

11.he: אִם־יַחֲלֹ֥ף וְיַסְגִּ֑יר וְ֝יַקְהִ֗יל וּמִ֣י יְשִׁיבֶֽנּוּ׃

lines.text: If he passes by, or confines, or convenes a court, then who can oppose him?
If He pass on, and shut up, and assemble, Who then dost reverse it?

11.he: כִּי־ה֭וּא יָדַ֣ע מְתֵי־שָׁ֑וְא וַיַּרְא־אָ֝֗וֶן וְלֹ֣א יִתְבּוֹנָֽן׃

lines.text: For he knows false men. He sees iniquity also, even though he doesn’t consider it.
For he hath known men of vanity, And He seeth iniquity, And one doth not consider [it]!

11.he: וְאִ֣ישׁ נָ֭בוּב יִלָּבֵ֑ב וְעַ֥יִר פֶּ֝֗רֶא אָדָ֥ם יִוָּלֵֽד׃

lines.text: An empty-headed man becomes wise when a man is born as a wild donkey’s colt.
And empty man is bold, And the colt of a wild ass man is born.

11.he: אִם־אַ֭תָּ֗ה הֲכִינ֣וֹתָ לִבֶּ֑ךָ וּפָרַשְׂתָּ֖ אֵלָ֣יו כַּפֶּֽךָ׃

lines.text: “If you set your heart aright, stretch out your hands toward him.
If thou — thou hast prepared thy heart, And hast spread out unto Him thy hands,

11.he: אִם־אָ֣וֶן בְּ֭יָדְךָ הַרְחִיקֵ֑הוּ וְאַל־תַּשְׁכֵּ֖ן בְּאֹהָלֶ֣יךָ עַוְלָֽה׃

lines.text: If iniquity is in your hand, put it far away. Don’t let unrighteousness dwell in your tents.
If iniquity [is] in thy hand, put it far off, And let not perverseness dwell in thy tents.

11.he: כִּי־אָ֤ז ׀ תִּשָּׂ֣א פָנֶ֣יךָ מִמּ֑וּם וְהָיִ֥יתָ מֻ֝צָ֗ק וְלֹ֣א תִירָֽא׃

lines.text: Surely then you will lift up your face without spot; Yes, you will be steadfast, and will not fear:
For then thou liftest up thy face from blemish, And thou hast been firm, and fearest not.

11.he: כִּי־אַ֭תָּה עָמָ֣ל תִּשְׁכָּ֑ח כְּמַ֖יִם עָבְר֣וּ תִזְכֹּֽר׃

lines.text: for you will forget your misery. You will remember it like waters that have passed away.
For thou dost forget misery, As waters passed away thou rememberest.

11.he: וּֽ֭מִצָּהֳרַיִם יָק֣וּם חָ֑לֶד תָּ֝עֻ֗פָה כַּבֹּ֥קֶר תִּהְיֶֽה׃

lines.text: Life will be clearer than the noonday. Though there is darkness, it will be as the morning.
And above the noon doth age rise, Thou fliest — as the morning thou art.

11.he: וּֽ֭בָטַחְתָּ כִּי־יֵ֣שׁ תִּקְוָ֑ה וְ֝חָפַרְתָּ֗ לָבֶ֥טַח תִּשְׁכָּֽב׃

lines.text: You will be secure, because there is hope. Yes, you will search, and will take your rest in safety.
And thou hast trusted because their is hope, And searched — in confidence thou liest down,

11.he: וְֽ֭רָבַצְתָּ וְאֵ֣ין מַחֲרִ֑יד וְחִלּ֖וּ פָנֶ֣יךָ רַבִּֽים׃

lines.text: Also you will lie down, and no one will make you afraid. Yes, many will court your favor.
And thou hast rested, And none is causing trembling, And many have entreated thy face;

11.he: וְעֵינֵ֥י רְשָׁעִ֗ים תִּ֫כְלֶ֥ינָה וּ֭מָנוֹס אָבַ֣ד מִנְהֶ֑ם וְ֝תִקְוָתָ֗ם מַֽפַּח־נָֽפֶשׁ׃

lines.text: But the eyes of the wicked will fail. They will have no way to flee. Their hope will be the giving up of the spirit.”
And the eyes of the wicked are consumed, And refuge hath perished from them, And their hope [is] a breathing out of soul!

12.he: וַיַּ֥עַן אִיּ֗וֹב וַיֹּאמַֽר׃

lines.text: Then Job answered,
And Job answereth and saith: —

12.he: אָ֭מְנָם כִּ֣י אַתֶּם־עָ֑ם וְ֝עִמָּכֶ֗ם תָּמ֥וּת חָכְמָֽה׃

lines.text: “No doubt, but you are the people, and wisdom will die with you.
Truly — ye [are] the people, And with you doth wisdom die.

12.he: גַּם־לִ֤י לֵבָ֨ב ׀ כְּֽמוֹכֶ֗ם לֹא־נֹפֵ֣ל אָנֹכִ֣י מִכֶּ֑ם וְאֶת־מִי־אֵ֥ין כְּמוֹ־אֵֽלֶּה׃

lines.text: But I have understanding as well as you; I am not inferior to you. Yes, who doesn’t know such things as these?
I also have a heart like you, I am not fallen more than you, And with whom is there not like these?

12.he: שְׂחֹ֤ק לְרֵעֵ֨הוּ ׀ אֶֽהְיֶ֗ה קֹרֵ֣א לֶ֭אֱלוֹהַּ וַֽיַּעֲנֵ֑הוּ שְׂ֝ח֗וֹק צַדִּ֥יק תָּמִֽים׃

lines.text: I am like one who is a joke to his neighbor, I, who called on God, and he answered. The just, the blameless man is a joke.
A laughter to his friend I am: 'He calleth to God, and He answereth him,' A laughter [is] the perfect righteous one.

12.he: לַפִּ֣יד בּ֭וּז לְעַשְׁתּ֣וּת שַׁאֲנָ֑ן נָ֝כ֗וֹן לְמ֣וֹעֲדֵי רָֽגֶל׃

lines.text: In the thought of him who is at ease there is contempt for misfortune. It is ready for them whose foot slips.
A torch — despised in the thoughts of the secure Is prepared for those sliding with the feet.

12.he: יִשְׁלָ֤יוּ אֹֽהָלִ֨ים ׀ לְשֹׁ֥דְדִ֗ים וּֽ֭בַטֻּחוֹת לְמַרְגִּ֣יזֵי אֵ֑ל לַאֲשֶׁ֤ר הֵבִ֖יא אֱל֣וֹהַּ בְּיָדֽוֹ׃

lines.text: The tents of robbers prosper. Those who provoke God are secure, who carry their god in their hands.
At peace are the tents of spoilers, And those provoking God have confidence, He into whose hand God hath brought.

12.he: וְֽאוּלָ֗ם שְׁאַל־נָ֣א בְהֵמ֣וֹת וְתֹרֶ֑ךָּ וְע֥וֹף הַ֝שָּׁמַ֗יִם וְיַגֶּד־לָֽךְ׃

lines.text: “But ask the animals, now, and they will teach you; the birds of the sky, and they will tell you.
And yet, ask, I pray thee, [One of] the beasts, and it doth shew thee, And a fowl of the heavens, And it doth declare to thee.

12.he: א֤וֹ שִׂ֣יחַ לָאָ֣רֶץ וְתֹרֶ֑ךָּ וִֽיסַפְּר֥וּ לְ֝ךָ֗ דְּגֵ֣י הַיָּֽם׃

lines.text: Or speak to the earth, and it will teach you. The fish of the sea will declare to you.
Or talk to the earth, and it sheweth thee, And fishes of the sea recount to thee:

12.he: מִ֭י לֹא־יָדַ֣ע בְּכָל־אֵ֑לֶּה כִּ֥י יַד־יְ֝הוָה עָ֣שְׂתָה זֹּֽאת׃

lines.text: Who doesn’t know that in all these, Yahweh’s hand has done this,
'Who hath not known in all these, That the hand of Jehovah hath done this?

12.he: אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּ֭יָדוֹ נֶ֣פֶשׁ כָּל־חָ֑י וְ֝ר֗וּחַ כָּל־בְּשַׂר־אִֽישׁ׃

lines.text: in whose hand is the life of every living thing, and the breath of all mankind?
In whose hand [is] the breath of every living thing, And the spirit of all flesh of man.'

12.he: הֲלֹא־אֹ֭זֶן מִלִּ֣ין תִּבְחָ֑ן וְ֝חֵ֗ךְ אֹ֣כֶל יִטְעַם־לֽוֹ׃

lines.text: Doesn’t the ear try words, even as the palate tastes its food?
Doth not the ear try words? And the palate taste food for itself?

12.he: בִּֽישִׁישִׁ֥ים חָכְמָ֑ה וְאֹ֖רֶךְ יָמִ֣ים תְּבוּנָֽה׃

lines.text: With aged men is wisdom, in length of days understanding.
With the very aged [is] wisdom, And [with] length of days understanding.

12.he: עִ֭מּוֹ חָכְמָ֣ה וּגְבוּרָ֑ה ל֝֗וֹ עֵצָ֥ה וּתְבוּנָֽה׃

lines.text: “With God is wisdom and might. He has counsel and understanding.
With Him [are] wisdom and might, To him [are] counsel and understanding.

12.he: הֵ֣ן יַ֭הֲרוֹס וְלֹ֣א יִבָּנֶ֑ה יִסְגֹּ֥ר עַל־אִ֝֗ישׁ וְלֹ֣א יִפָּתֵֽחַ׃

lines.text: Behold, he breaks down, and it can’t be built again. He imprisons a man, and there can be no release.
Lo, He breaketh down, and it is not built up, He shutteth against a man, And it is not opened.

12.he: הֵ֤ן יַעְצֹ֣ר בַּמַּ֣יִם וְיִבָ֑שׁוּ וִֽ֝ישַׁלְּחֵ֗ם וְיַ֖הַפְכוּ אָֽרֶץ׃

lines.text: Behold, he withholds the waters, and they dry up. Again, he sends them out, and they overturn the earth.
Lo, He keepeth in the waters, and they are dried up, And he sendeth them forth, And they overturn the land.

12.he: עִ֭מּוֹ עֹ֣ז וְתֽוּשִׁיָּ֑ה ל֝֗וֹ שֹׁגֵ֥ג וּמַשְׁגֶּֽה׃

lines.text: With him is strength and wisdom. The deceived and the deceiver are his.
With Him [are] strength and wisdom, His the deceived and deceiver.

12.he: מוֹלִ֣יךְ יוֹעֲצִ֣ים שׁוֹלָ֑ל וְֽשֹׁפְטִ֥ים יְהוֹלֵֽל׃

lines.text: He leads counselors away stripped. He makes judges fools.
Causing counsellors to go away a spoil, And judges He maketh foolish.

12.he: מוּסַ֣ר מְלָכִ֣ים פִּתֵּ֑חַ וַיֶּאְסֹ֥ר אֵ֝ז֗וֹר בְּמָתְנֵיהֶֽם׃

lines.text: He loosens the bond of kings. He binds their waist with a belt.
The bands of kings He hath opened, And He bindeth a girdle on their loins.

12.he: מוֹלִ֣יךְ כֹּהֲנִ֣ים שׁוֹלָ֑ל וְאֵ֖תָנִ֣ים יְסַלֵּֽף׃

lines.text: He leads priests away stripped, and overthrows the mighty.
Causing ministers to go away a spoil And strong ones He overthroweth.

12.he: מֵסִ֣יר שָׂ֭פָה לְנֶאֱמָנִ֑ים וְטַ֖עַם זְקֵנִ֣ים יִקָּֽח׃

lines.text: He removes the speech of those who are trusted, and takes away the understanding of the elders.
Turning aside the lip of the stedfast, And the reason of the aged He taketh away.

12.he: שׁוֹפֵ֣ךְ בּ֭וּז עַל־נְדִיבִ֑ים וּמְזִ֖יחַ אֲפִיקִ֣ים רִפָּֽה׃

lines.text: He pours contempt on princes, and loosens the belt of the strong.
Pouring contempt upon princes, And the girdle of the mighty He made feeble.

12.he: מְגַלֶּ֣ה עֲ֭מֻקוֹת מִנִּי־חֹ֑שֶׁךְ וַיֹּצֵ֖א לָא֣וֹר צַלְמָֽוֶת׃

lines.text: He uncovers deep things out of darkness, and brings out to light the shadow of death.
Removing deep things out of darkness, And He bringeth out to light death-shade.

12.he: מַשְׂגִּ֣יא לַ֭גּוֹיִם וַֽיְאַבְּדֵ֑ם שֹׁטֵ֥חַ לַ֝גּוֹיִ֗ם וַיַּנְחֵֽם׃

lines.text: He increases the nations, and he destroys them. He enlarges the nations, and he leads them captive.
Magnifying the nations, and He destroyeth them, Spreading out the nations, and He quieteth them.

12.he: מֵסִ֗יר לֵ֭ב רָאשֵׁ֣י עַם־הָאָ֑רֶץ וַ֝יַּתְעֵ֗ם בְּתֹ֣הוּ לֹא־דָֽרֶךְ׃

lines.text: He takes away understanding from the chiefs of the people of the earth, and causes them to wander in a wilderness where there is no way.
Turning aside the heart Of the heads of the people of the land, And he causeth them to wander In vacancy — no way!

12.he: יְמַֽשְׁשׁוּ־חֹ֥שֶׁךְ וְלֹא־א֑וֹר וַ֝יַּתְעֵ֗ם כַּשִּׁכּֽוֹר׃

lines.text: They grope in the dark without light. He makes them stagger like a drunken man.
They feel darkness, and not light, He causeth them to wander as a drunkard.

13.he: הֶן־כֹּ֭ל רָאֲתָ֣ה עֵינִ֑י שָֽׁמְעָ֥ה אָ֝זְנִ֗י וַתָּ֥בֶן לָֽהּ׃
