lines.text: Now men don’t see the light which is bright in the skies, but the wind passes, and clears them.
And now, they have not seen the light, Bright it [is] in the clouds, And the wind hath passed by and cleanseth them.

37.he: מִ֭צָּפוֹן זָהָ֣ב יֶֽאֱתֶ֑ה עַל־אֱ֝ל֗וֹהַּ נ֣וֹרָא הֽוֹד׃

lines.text: Out of the north comes golden splendor. With God is awesome majesty.
From the golden north it cometh, Beside God [is] fearful honour.

37.he: שַׁדַּ֣י לֹֽא־מְ֭צָאנֻהוּ שַׂגִּיא־כֹ֑חַ וּמִשְׁפָּ֥ט וְרֹב־צְ֝דָקָ֗ה לֹ֣א יְעַנֶּֽה׃

lines.text: We can’t reach the Almighty. He is exalted in power. In justice and great righteousness, he will not oppress.
The Mighty! we have not found Him out, High in power and judgment, He doth not answer! And abundant in righteousness,

37.he: לָ֭כֵן יְרֵא֣וּהוּ אֲנָשִׁ֑ים לֹֽא־יִ֝רְאֶ֗ה כָּל־חַכְמֵי־לֵֽב׃

lines.text: Therefore men revere him. He doesn’t regard any who are wise of heart.”
Therefore do men fear Him, He seeth not any of the wise of heart.

38.he: וַיַּֽעַן־יְהוָ֣ה אֶת־אִ֭יּוֹב מנ הסערה וַיֹּאמַֽר׃

lines.text: Then Yahweh answered Job out of the whirlwind,
And Jehovah answereth Job out of the whirlwind, and saith: —

38.he: מִ֤י זֶ֨ה ׀ מַחְשִׁ֖יךְ עֵצָ֥ה בְמִלִּ֗ין בְּֽלִי־דָֽעַת׃

lines.text: “Who is this who darkens counsel by words without knowledge?
Who [is] this — darkening counsel, By words without knowledge?

38.he: אֱזָר־נָ֣א כְגֶ֣בֶר חֲלָצֶ֑יךָ וְ֝אֶשְׁאָלְךָ֗ וְהוֹדִיעֵֽנִי׃

lines.text: Brace yourself like a man, for I will question you, then you answer me!
Gird, I pray thee, as a man, thy loins, And I ask thee, and cause thou Me to know.

38.he: אֵיפֹ֣ה הָ֭יִיתָ בְּיָסְדִי־אָ֑רֶץ הַ֝גֵּ֗ד אִם־יָדַ֥עְתָּ בִינָֽה׃

lines.text: “Where were you when I laid the foundations of the earth? Declare, if you have understanding.
Where wast thou when I founded earth? Declare, if thou hast known understanding.

38.he: מִי־שָׂ֣ם מְ֭מַדֶּיהָ כִּ֣י תֵדָ֑ע א֤וֹ מִֽי־נָטָ֖ה עָלֶ֣יהָ קָּֽו׃

lines.text: Who determined its measures, if you know? Or who stretched the line on it?
Who placed its measures — if thou knowest? Or who hath stretched out upon it a line?

38.he: עַל־מָ֭ה אֲדָנֶ֣יהָ הָטְבָּ֑עוּ א֥וֹ מִֽי־יָ֝רָ֗ה אֶ֣בֶן פִּנָּתָֽהּ׃

lines.text: What were its foundations fastened on? Or who laid its cornerstone,
On what have its sockets been sunk? Or who hath cast its corner-stone?

38.he: בְּרָן־יַ֭חַד כּ֣וֹכְבֵי בֹ֑קֶר וַ֝יָּרִ֗יעוּ כָּל־בְּנֵ֥י אֱלֹהִֽים׃

lines.text: when the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted for joy?
In the singing together of stars of morning, And all sons of God shout for joy,

38.he: וַיָּ֣סֶךְ בִּדְלָתַ֣יִם יָ֑ם בְּ֝גִיח֗וֹ מֵרֶ֥חֶם יֵצֵֽא׃

lines.text: “Or who shut up the sea with doors, when it broke out of the womb,
And He shutteth up with doors the sea, In its coming forth, from the womb it goeth out.

38.he: בְּשׂוּמִ֣י עָנָ֣ן לְבֻשׁ֑וֹ וַ֝עֲרָפֶ֗ל חֲתֻלָּתֽוֹ׃

lines.text: when I made clouds its garment, and wrapped it in thick darkness,
In My making a cloud its clothing, And thick darkness its swaddling band,

38.he: וָאֶשְׁבֹּ֣ר עָלָ֣יו חֻקִּ֑י וָֽ֝אָשִׂ֗ים בְּרִ֣יחַ וּדְלָתָֽיִם׃

lines.text: marked out for it my bound, set bars and doors,
And I measure over it My statute, And place bar and doors,

38.he: וָאֹמַ֗ר עַד־פֹּ֣ה תָ֭בוֹא וְלֹ֣א תֹסִ֑יף וּפֹ֥א־יָ֝שִׁ֗ית בִּגְא֥וֹן גַּלֶּֽיךָ׃

lines.text: and said, ‘You may come here, but no further. Your proud waves shall be stopped here?’
And say, 'Hitherto come thou, and add not, And a command is placed On the pride of thy billows.'

38.he: הְֽ֭מִיָּמֶיךָ צִוִּ֣יתָ בֹּ֑קֶר ידעתה שחר מְקֹמֽוֹ׃

lines.text: “Have you commanded the morning in your days, and caused the dawn to know its place,
Hast thou commanded morning since thy days? Causest thou the dawn to know its place?

38.he: לֶ֭אֱחֹז בְּכַנְפ֣וֹת הָאָ֑רֶץ וְיִנָּעֲר֖וּ רְשָׁעִ֣ים מִמֶּֽנָּה׃

lines.text: that it might take hold of the ends of the earth, and shake the wicked out of it?
To take hold on the skirts of the earth, And the wicked are shaken out of it,

38.he: תִּ֭תְהַפֵּךְ כְּחֹ֣מֶר חוֹתָ֑ם וְ֝יִֽתְיַצְּב֗וּ כְּמ֣וֹ לְבֽוּשׁ׃

lines.text: It is changed as clay under the seal, and presented as a garment.
It turneth itself as clay of a seal And they station themselves as clothed.

38.he: וְיִמָּנַ֣ע מֵרְשָׁעִ֣ים אוֹרָ֑ם וּזְר֥וֹעַ רָ֝מָ֗ה תִּשָּׁבֵֽר׃

lines.text: From the wicked, their light is withheld. The high arm is broken.
And withheld from the wicked is their light, And the arm lifted up is broken.

38.he: הֲ֭בָאתָ עַד־נִבְכֵי־יָ֑ם וּבְחֵ֥קֶר תְּ֝ה֗וֹם הִתְהַלָּֽכְתָּ׃

lines.text: “Have you entered into the springs of the sea? Or have you walked in the recesses of the deep?
Hast thou come in to springs of the sea? And in searching the deep Hast thou walked up and down?

38.he: הֲנִגְל֣וּ לְ֭ךָ שַׁעֲרֵי־מָ֑וֶת וְשַׁעֲרֵ֖י צַלְמָ֣וֶת תִּרְאֶֽה׃

lines.text: Have the gates of death been revealed to you? Or have you seen the gates of the shadow of death?
Revealed to thee were the gates of death? And the gates of death-shade dost thou see?

38.he: הִ֭תְבֹּנַנְתָּ עַד־רַחֲבֵי־אָ֑רֶץ הַ֝גֵּ֗ד אִם־יָדַ֥עְתָּ כֻלָּֽהּ׃

lines.text: Have you comprehended the earth in its width? Declare, if you know it all.
Thou hast understanding, Even unto the broad places of earth! Declare — if thou hast known it all.

38.he: אֵי־זֶ֣ה הַ֭דֶּרֶךְ יִשְׁכָּן־א֑וֹר וְ֝חֹ֗שֶׁךְ אֵי־זֶ֥ה מְקֹמֽוֹ׃

lines.text: “What is the way to the dwelling of light? As for darkness, where is its place,
Where [is] this — the way light dwelleth? And darkness, where [is] this — its place?

38.he: כִּ֣י תִ֭קָּחֶנּוּ אֶל־גְּבוּל֑וֹ וְכִֽי־תָ֝בִין נְתִיב֥וֹת בֵּיתֽוֹ׃

lines.text: that you should take it to its bound, that you should discern the paths to its house?
That thou dost take it unto its boundary, And that thou dost understand The paths of its house.

38.he: יָ֭דַעְתָּ כִּי־אָ֣ז תִּוָּלֵ֑ד וּמִסְפַּ֖ר יָמֶ֣יךָ רַבִּֽים׃

lines.text: Surely you know, for you were born then, and the number of your days is great!
Thou hast known — for then thou art born And the number of thy days [are] many!

38.he: הֲ֭בָאתָ אֶל־אֹצְר֣וֹת שָׁ֑לֶג וְאֹצְר֖וֹת בָּרָ֣ד תִּרְאֶֽה׃

lines.text: Have you entered the treasuries of the snow, or have you seen the treasures of the hail,
Hast thou come in unto the treasure of snow? Yea, the treasures of hail dost thou see?

38.he: אֲשֶׁר־חָשַׂ֥כְתִּי לְעֶת־צָ֑ר לְי֥וֹם קְ֝רָ֗ב וּמִלְחָמָֽה׃

lines.text: which I have reserved against the time of trouble, against the day of battle and war?
That I have kept back for a time of distress, For a day of conflict and battle.

38.he: אֵי־זֶ֣ה הַ֭דֶּרֶךְ יֵחָ֣לֶק א֑וֹר יָפֵ֖ץ קָדִ֣ים עֲלֵי־אָֽרֶץ׃

lines.text: By what way is the lightning distributed, or the east wind scattered on the earth?
Where [is] this, the way light is apportioned? It scattereth an east wind over the earth.

38.he: מִֽי־פִלַּ֣ג לַשֶּׁ֣טֶף תְּעָלָ֑ה וְ֝דֶ֗רֶךְ לַחֲזִ֥יז קֹלֽוֹת׃

lines.text: Who has cut a channel for the flood water, or the path for the thunder storm,
Who hath divided for the flood a conduit? And a way for the lightning of the voices?

38.he: לְ֭הַמְטִיר עַל־אֶ֣רֶץ לֹא־אִ֑ישׁ מִ֝דְבָּ֗ר לֹא־אָדָ֥ם בּֽוֹ׃

lines.text: to cause it to rain on a land where there is no man, on the wilderness, in which there is no man,
To cause [it] to rain on a land — no man, A wilderness — no man in it.

38.he: לְהַשְׂבִּ֣יעַ שֹׁ֭אָה וּמְשֹׁאָ֑ה וּ֝לְהַצְמִ֗יחַ מֹ֣צָא דֶֽשֶׁא׃

lines.text: to satisfy the waste and desolate ground, to cause the tender grass to grow?
To satisfy a desolate and waste place, And to cause to shoot up The produce of the tender grass?

38.he: הֲיֵשׁ־לַמָּטָ֥ר אָ֑ב א֥וֹ מִי־ה֝וֹלִ֗יד אֶגְלֵי־טָֽל׃

lines.text: Does the rain have a father? Or who fathers the drops of dew?
Hath the rain a father? Or who hath begotten the drops of dew?

38.he: מִבֶּ֣טֶן מִ֭י יָצָ֣א הַקָּ֑רַח וּכְפֹ֥ר שָׁ֝מַיִם מִ֣י יְלָדֽוֹ׃

lines.text: Whose womb did the ice come out of? Who has given birth to the gray frost of the sky?
From whose belly came forth the ice? And the hoar-frost of the heavens, Who hath begotten it?

38.he: כָּ֭אֶבֶן מַ֣יִם יִתְחַבָּ֑אוּ וּפְנֵ֥י תְ֝ה֗וֹם יִתְלַכָּֽדוּ׃

lines.text: The waters become hard like stone, when the surface of the deep is frozen.
As a stone waters are hidden, And the face of the deep is captured.

38.he: הַֽ֭תְקַשֵּׁר מַעֲדַנּ֣וֹת כִּימָ֑ה אֽוֹ־מֹשְׁכ֖וֹת כְּסִ֣יל תְּפַתֵּֽחַ׃

lines.text: “Can you bind the cluster of the Pleiades, or loosen the cords of Orion?
Dost thou bind sweet influences of Kimah? Or the attractions of Kesil dost thou open?

38.he: הֲתֹצִ֣יא מַזָּר֣וֹת בְּעִתּ֑וֹ וְ֝עַ֗יִשׁ עַל־בָּנֶ֥יהָ תַנְחֵֽם׃

lines.text: Can you lead the constellations out in their season? Or can you guide the Bear with her cubs?
Dost thou bring out Mazzaroth in its season? And Aysh for her sons dost thou comfort?

38.he: הֲ֭יָדַעְתָּ חֻקּ֣וֹת שָׁמָ֑יִם אִם־תָּשִׂ֖ים מִשְׁטָר֣וֹ בָאָֽרֶץ׃

lines.text: Do you know the laws of the heavens? Can you establish its dominion over the earth?
Hast thou known the statutes of heaven? Or dost thou appoint Its dominion in the earth?

38.he: הֲתָרִ֣ים לָעָ֣ב קוֹלֶ֑ךָ וְֽשִׁפְעַת־מַ֥יִם תְּכַסֶּֽךָּ׃

lines.text: “Can you lift up your voice to the clouds, That abundance of waters may cover you?
Dost thou lift up to the cloud thy voice, And abundance of water doth cover thee?

38.he: הַֽתְשַׁלַּ֣ח בְּרָקִ֣ים וְיֵלֵ֑כוּ וְיֹאמְר֖וּ לְךָ֣ הִנֵּֽנוּ׃

lines.text: Can you send out lightnings, that they may go? Do they report to you, ‘Here we are?’
Dost thou send out lightnings, and they go And say unto thee, 'Behold us?'

38.he: מִי־שָׁ֭ת בַּטֻּח֣וֹת חָכְמָ֑ה א֤וֹ מִֽי־נָתַ֖ן לַשֶּׂ֣כְוִי בִינָֽה׃

lines.text: Who has put wisdom in the inward parts? Or who has given understanding to the mind?
Who hath put in the inward parts wisdom? Or who hath given To the covered part understanding?

38.he: מִֽי־יְסַפֵּ֣ר שְׁחָקִ֣ים בְּחָכְמָ֑ה וְנִבְלֵ֥י שָׁ֝מַ֗יִם מִ֣י יַשְׁכִּֽיב׃

lines.text: Who can count the clouds by wisdom? Or who can pour out the containers of the sky,
Who doth number the clouds by wisdom? And the bottles of the heavens, Who doth cause to lie down,

38.he: בְּצֶ֣קֶת עָ֭פָר לַמּוּצָ֑ק וּרְגָבִ֥ים יְדֻבָּֽקוּ׃

lines.text: when the dust runs into a mass, and the clods of earth stick together?
In the hardening of dust into hardness, And clods cleave together?

38.he: הֲתָצ֣וּד לְלָבִ֣יא טָ֑רֶף וְחַיַּ֖ת כְּפִירִ֣ים תְּמַלֵּֽא׃

lines.text: “Can you hunt the prey for the lioness, or satisfy the appetite of the young lions,
Dost thou hunt for a lion prey? And the desire of young lions fulfil?

38.he: כִּי־יָשֹׁ֥חוּ בַמְּעוֹנ֑וֹת יֵשְׁב֖וּ בַסֻּכָּ֣ה לְמוֹ־אָֽרֶב׃

lines.text: when they crouch in their dens, and lie in wait in the thicket?
When they bow down in dens — Abide in a thicket for a covert?

38.he: מִ֤י יָכִ֥ין לָעֹרֵ֗ב צֵ֫יד֥וֹ כִּֽי־ילדו אֶל־אֵ֣ל יְשַׁוֵּ֑עוּ יִ֝תְע֗וּ לִבְלִי־אֹֽכֶל׃

lines.text: Who provides for the raven his prey, when his young ones cry to God, and wander for lack of food?
Who doth prepare for a raven his provision, When his young ones cry unto God? They wander without food.

39.he: הֲיָדַ֗עְתָּ עֵ֭ת לֶ֣דֶת יַעֲלֵי־סָ֑לַע חֹלֵ֖ל אַיָּל֣וֹת תִּשְׁמֹֽר׃

lines.text: “Do you know the time when the mountain goats give birth? Do you watch when the doe bears fawns?
Hast thou known the time of The bearing of the wild goats of the rock? The bringing forth of hinds thou dost mark!

39.he: תִּסְפֹּ֣ר יְרָחִ֣ים תְּמַלֶּ֑אנָה וְ֝יָדַ֗עְתָּ עֵ֣ת לִדְתָּֽנָה׃

lines.text: Can you count the months that they fulfill? Or do you know the time when they give birth?
Thou dost number the months they fulfil? And thou hast known the time of their bringing forth!

39.he: תִּ֭כְרַעְנָה יַלְדֵיהֶ֣ן תְּפַלַּ֑חְנָה חֶבְלֵיהֶ֥ם תְּשַׁלַּֽחְנָה׃

lines.text: They bow themselves. They bear their young. They end their labor pains.
They bow down, Their young ones they bring forth safely, Their pangs they cast forth.

39.he: יַחְלְמ֣וּ בְ֭נֵיהֶם יִרְבּ֣וּ בַבָּ֑ר יָ֝צְא֗וּ וְלֹא־שָׁ֥בוּ לָֽמוֹ׃

lines.text: Their young ones become strong. They grow up in the open field. They go out, and don’t return again.
Safe are their young ones, They grow up in the field, they have gone out, And have not returned to them.

39.he: מִֽי־שִׁלַּ֣ח פֶּ֣רֶא חָפְשִׁ֑י וּמֹסְר֥וֹת עָ֝ר֗וֹד מִ֣י פִתֵּֽחַ׃

lines.text: “Who has set the wild donkey free? Or who has loosened the bonds of the swift donkey,
Who hath sent forth the wild ass free? Yea, the bands of the wild ass who opened?

39.he: אֲשֶׁר־שַׂ֣מְתִּי עֲרָבָ֣ה בֵית֑וֹ וּֽמִשְׁכְּנוֹתָ֥יו מְלֵֽחָה׃

lines.text: whose home I have made the wilderness, and the salt land his dwelling place?
Whose house I have made the wilderness, And his dwellings the barren land,

39.he: יִ֭שְׂחַק לַהֲמ֣וֹן קִרְיָ֑ה תְּשֻׁא֥וֹת נ֝וֹגֵ֗שׂ לֹ֣א יִשְׁמָֽע׃

lines.text: He scorns the tumult of the city, neither does he hear the shouting of the driver.
He doth laugh at the multitude of a city, The cries of an exactor he heareth not.

39.he: יְת֣וּר הָרִ֣ים מִרְעֵ֑הוּ וְאַחַ֖ר כָּל־יָר֣וֹק יִדְרֽוֹשׁ׃

lines.text: The range of the mountains is his pasture, He searches after every green thing.
The range of mountains [is] his pasture, And after every green thing he seeketh.

39.he: הֲיֹ֣אבֶה רֵּ֣ים עָבְדֶ֑ךָ אִם־יָ֝לִ֗ין עַל־אֲבוּסֶֽךָ׃

lines.text: “Will the wild ox be content to serve you? Or will he stay by your feeding trough?
Is a Reem willing to serve thee? Doth he lodge by thy crib?

39.he: הֲֽתִקְשָׁר־רֵ֭ים בְּתֶ֣לֶם עֲבֹת֑וֹ אִם־יְשַׂדֵּ֖ד עֲמָקִ֣ים אַחֲרֶֽיךָ׃

lines.text: Can you hold the wild ox in the furrow with his harness? Or will he till the valleys after you?
Dost thou bind a Reem in a furrow [with] his thick band? Doth he harrow valleys after thee?

39.he: הֲֽתִבְטַח־בּ֭וֹ כִּי־רַ֣ב כֹּח֑וֹ וְתַעֲזֹ֖ב אֵלָ֣יו יְגִיעֶֽךָ׃

lines.text: Will you trust him, because his strength is great? Or will you leave to him your labor?
Dost thou trust in him because great [is] his power? And dost thou leave unto him thy labour?

39.he: הֲתַאֲמִ֣ין בּ֭וֹ כִּי־ישוב זַרְעֶ֑ךָ וְֽגָרְנְךָ֥ יֶאֱסֹֽף׃

lines.text: Will you confide in him, that he will bring home your seed, and gather the grain of your threshing floor?
Dost thou trust in him That he doth bring back thy seed? And [to] thy threshing-floor doth gather [it]?

39.he: כְּנַף־רְנָנִ֥ים נֶעֱלָ֑סָה אִם־אֶ֝בְרָ֗ה חֲסִידָ֥ה וְנֹצָֽה׃

lines.text: “The wings of the ostrich wave proudly; but are they the feathers and plumage of love?
The wing of the rattling ones exulteth, Whether the pinion of the ostrich or hawk.

39.he: כִּֽי־תַעֲזֹ֣ב לָאָ֣רֶץ בֵּצֶ֑יהָ וְֽעַל־עָפָ֥ר תְּחַמֵּֽם׃

lines.text: For she leaves her eggs on the earth, warms them in the dust,
For she leaveth on the earth her eggs, And on the dust she doth warm them,

39.he: וַ֭תִּשְׁכַּח כִּי־רֶ֣גֶל תְּזוּרֶ֑הָ וְחַיַּ֖ת הַשָּׂדֶ֣ה תְּדוּשֶֽׁהָ׃

lines.text: and forgets that the foot may crush them, or that the wild animal may trample them.
And she forgetteth that a foot may press it, And a beast of the field tread it down.

39.he: הִקְשִׁ֣יחַ בָּנֶ֣יהָ לְּלֹא־לָ֑הּ לְרִ֖יק יְגִיעָ֣הּ בְּלִי־פָֽחַד׃

lines.text: She deals harshly with her young ones, as if they were not hers. Though her labor is in vain, she is without fear,
Her young ones it hath hardened without her, In vain [is] her labour without fear.

39.he: כִּֽי־הִשָּׁ֣הּ אֱל֣וֹהַּ חָכְמָ֑ה וְלֹא־חָ֥לַק לָ֝֗הּ בַּבִּינָֽה׃

lines.text: because God has deprived her of wisdom, neither has he imparted to her understanding.
For God hath caused her to forget wisdom, And He hath not given a portion To her in understanding:

39.he: כָּ֭עֵת בַּמָּר֣וֹם תַּמְרִ֑יא תִּֽשְׂחַ֥ק לַ֝סּ֗וּס וּלְרֹֽכְבֽוֹ׃

lines.text: When she lifts up herself on high, she scorns the horse and his rider.
At the time on high she lifteth herself up, She laugheth at the horse and at his rider.

39.he: הֲתִתֵּ֣ן לַסּ֣וּס גְּבוּרָ֑ה הֲתַלְבִּ֖ישׁ צַוָּאר֣וֹ רַעְמָֽה׃

lines.text: “Have you given the horse might? Have you clothed his neck with a quivering mane?
Dost thou give to the horse might? Dost thou clothe his neck [with] a mane?

39.he: הְֽ֭תַרְעִישֶׁנּוּ כָּאַרְבֶּ֑ה ה֖וֹד נַחְר֣וֹ אֵימָֽה׃

lines.text: Have you made him to leap as a locust? The glory of his snorting is awesome.
Dost thou cause him to rush as a locust? The majesty of his snorting [is] terrible.

39.he: יַחְפְּר֣וּ בָ֭עֵמֶק וְיָשִׂ֣ישׂ בְּכֹ֑חַ יֵ֝צֵ֗א לִקְרַאת־נָֽשֶׁק׃

lines.text: He paws in the valley, and rejoices in his strength. He goes out to meet the armed men.
They dig in a valley, and he rejoiceth in power, He goeth forth to meet the armour.

39.he: יִשְׂחַ֣ק לְ֭פַחַד וְלֹ֣א יֵחָ֑ת וְלֹֽא־יָ֝שׁ֗וּב מִפְּנֵי־חָֽרֶב׃

lines.text: He mocks at fear, and is not dismayed, neither does he turn back from the sword.
He laugheth at fear, and is not affrighted, And he turneth not back from the face of the sword.

39.he: עָ֭לָיו תִּרְנֶ֣ה אַשְׁפָּ֑ה לַ֖הַב חֲנִ֣ית וְכִידֽוֹן׃

lines.text: The quiver rattles against him, the flashing spear and the javelin.
Against him rattle doth quiver, The flame of a spear, and a halbert.

39.he: בְּרַ֣עַשׁ וְ֭רֹגֶז יְגַמֶּא־אָ֑רֶץ וְלֹֽא־יַ֝אֲמִ֗ין כִּי־ק֥וֹל שׁוֹפָֽר׃

lines.text: He eats up the ground with fierceness and rage, neither does he stand still at the sound of the trumpet.
With trembling and rage he swalloweth the ground, And remaineth not stedfast Because of the sound of a trumpet.

39.he: בְּדֵ֤י שֹׁפָ֨ר ׀ יֹ֘אמַ֤ר הֶאָ֗ח וּֽ֭מֵרָחוֹק יָרִ֣יחַ מִלְחָמָ֑ה רַ֥עַם שָׂ֝רִים וּתְרוּעָֽה׃

lines.text: As often as the trumpet sounds he snorts, ‘Aha!’ He smells the battle afar off, the thunder of the captains, and the shouting.
Among the trumpets he saith, Aha, And from afar he doth smell battle, Roaring of princes and shouting.

39.he: הֲֽ֭מִבִּינָ֣תְךָ יַֽאֲבֶר־נֵ֑ץ יִפְרֹ֖שׂ כנפו לְתֵימָֽן׃

lines.text: “Is it by your wisdom that the hawk soars, and stretches her wings toward the south?
By thine understanding flieth a hawk? Spreadeth he his wings to the south?

39.he: אִם־עַל־פִּ֭יךָ יַגְבִּ֣יהַּ נָ֑שֶׁר וְ֝כִ֗י יָרִ֥ים קִנּֽוֹ׃

lines.text: Is it at your command that the eagle mounts up, and makes his nest on high?
At thy command goeth an eagle up high? Or lifteth he up his nest?

39.he: סֶ֣לַע יִ֭שְׁכֹּן וְיִתְלֹנָ֑ן עַ֥ל־שֶׁן־סֶ֝֗לַע וּמְצוּדָֽה׃

lines.text: On the cliff he dwells, and makes his home, on the point of the cliff, and the stronghold.
A rock he doth inhabit, Yea, he lodgeth on the tooth of a rock, and fortress.

39.he: מִשָּׁ֥ם חָֽפַר־אֹ֑כֶל לְ֝מֵרָח֗וֹק עֵינָ֥יו יַבִּֽיטוּ׃

lines.text: From there he spies out the prey. His eyes see it afar off.
From thence he hath sought food, To a far off place his eyes look attentively,

39.he: וְאֶפְרֹחָ֥ו יְעַלְעוּ־דָ֑ם וּבַאֲשֶׁ֥ר חֲ֝לָלִ֗ים שָׁ֣ם הֽוּא׃

lines.text: His young ones also suck up blood. Where the slain are, there he is.”
And his brood gulp up blood, And where the pierced [are] — there [is] he!

40.he: וַיַּ֖עַן יְהוָ֥ה אֶת־אִיּ֗וֹב וַיֹּאמַֽר׃

lines.text: Moreover Yahweh answered Job,
And Jehovah doth answer Job, and saith: —

40.he: הֲ֭רֹב עִם־שַׁדַּ֣י יִסּ֑וֹר מוֹכִ֖יחַ אֱל֣וֹהַּ יַעֲנֶֽנָּה׃

lines.text: “Shall he who argues contend with the Almighty? He who argues with God, let him answer it.”
Is the striver with the Mighty instructed? The reprover of God, let him answer it.

40.he: וַיַּ֖עַן אִיּ֥וֹב אֶת־יְהוָ֗ה וַיֹּאמַֽר׃

lines.text: Then Job answered Yahweh,
And Job answereth Jehovah, and saith: —

40.he: הֵ֣ן קַ֭לֹּתִי מָ֣ה אֲשִׁיבֶ֑ךָּ יָ֝דִ֗י שַׂ֣מְתִּי לְמוֹ־פִֽי׃

lines.text: “Behold, I am of small account. What will I answer you? I lay my hand on my mouth.
Lo, I have been vile, What do I return to Thee? My hand I have placed on my mouth.

40.he: אַחַ֣ת דִּ֭בַּרְתִּי וְלֹ֣א אֶֽעֱנֶ֑ה וּ֝שְׁתַּ֗יִם וְלֹ֣א אוֹסִֽיף׃

lines.text: I have spoken once, and I will not answer; Yes, twice, but I will proceed no further.”
Once I have spoken, and I answer not, And twice, and I add not.

40.he: וַיַּֽעַן־יְהוָ֣ה אֶת־אִ֭יּוֹב מנ סערה וַיֹּאמַֽר׃

lines.text: Then Yahweh answered Job out of the whirlwind,
And Jehovah answereth Job out of the whirlwind, and saith: —

40.he: אֱזָר־נָ֣א כְגֶ֣בֶר חֲלָצֶ֑יךָ אֶ֝שְׁאָלְךָ֗ וְהוֹדִיעֵֽנִי׃

lines.text: “Now brace yourself like a man. I will question you, and you will answer me.
Gird, I pray thee, as a man, thy loins, I ask thee, and cause thou Me to know.

40.he: הַ֭אַף תָּפֵ֣ר מִשְׁפָּטִ֑י תַּ֝רְשִׁיעֵ֗נִי לְמַ֣עַן תִּצְדָּֽק׃

lines.text: Will you even annul my judgment? Will you condemn me, that you may be justified?
Dost thou also make void My judgment? Dost thou condemn Me, That thou mayest be righteous?

40.he: וְאִם־זְר֖וֹעַ כָּאֵ֥ל ׀ לָ֑ךְ וּ֝בְק֗וֹל כָּמֹ֥הוּ תַרְעֵֽם׃

lines.text: Or do you have an arm like God? Can you thunder with a voice like him?
And an arm like God hast thou? And with a voice like Him dost thou thunder?

40.he: עֲדֵ֥ה נָ֣א גָֽא֣וֹן וָגֹ֑בַהּ וְה֖וֹד וְהָדָ֣ר תִּלְבָּֽשׁ׃

lines.text: “Now deck yourself with excellency and dignity. Array yourself with honor and majesty.
Put on, I pray thee, excellency and loftiness, Yea, honour and beauty put on.

40.he: הָ֭פֵץ עֶבְר֣וֹת אַפֶּ֑ךָ וּרְאֵ֥ה כָל־גֵּ֝אֶ֗ה וְהַשְׁפִּילֵֽהוּ׃

lines.text: Pour out the fury of your anger. Look at everyone who is proud, and bring him low.
Scatter abroad the wrath of thine anger, And see every proud one, and make him low.

40.he: רְאֵ֣ה כָל־גֵּ֭אֶה הַכְנִיעֵ֑הוּ וַהֲדֹ֖ךְ רְשָׁעִ֣ים תַּחְתָּֽם׃

lines.text: Look at everyone who is proud, and humble him. Crush the wicked in their place.
See every proud one — humble him, And tread down the wicked in their place.

40.he: טָמְנֵ֣ם בֶּעָפָ֣ר יָ֑חַד פְּ֝נֵיהֶ֗ם חֲבֹ֣שׁ בַּטָּמֽוּן׃

lines.text: Hide them in the dust together. Bind their faces in the hidden place.
Hide them in the dust together, Their faces bind in secret.

40.he: וְגַם־אֲנִ֥י אוֹדֶ֑ךָּ כִּֽי־תוֹשִׁ֖עַ לְךָ֣ יְמִינֶֽךָ׃

lines.text: Then I will also admit to you that your own right hand can save you.
And even I — I do praise thee, For thy right hand giveth salvation to thee.

40.he: הִנֵּה־נָ֣א בְ֭הֵמוֹת אֲשֶׁר־עָשִׂ֣יתִי עִמָּ֑ךְ חָ֝צִ֗יר כַּבָּקָ֥ר יֹאכֵֽל׃

lines.text: “See now, behemoth, which I made as well as you. He eats grass as an ox.
Lo, I pray thee, Behemoth, that I made with thee: Grass as an ox he eateth.

40.he: הִנֵּה־נָ֣א כֹח֣וֹ בְמָתְנָ֑יו וְ֝אֹנ֗וֹ בִּשְׁרִירֵ֥י בִטְנֽוֹ׃

lines.text: Look now, his strength is in his thighs. His force is in the muscles of his belly.
Lo, I pray thee, his power [is] in his loins, And his strength in the muscles of his belly.

40.he: יַחְפֹּ֣ץ זְנָב֣וֹ כְמוֹ־אָ֑רֶז גִּידֵ֖י פחדו יְשֹׂרָֽגוּ׃

lines.text: He moves his tail like a cedar. The sinews of his thighs are knit together.
He doth bend his tail as a cedar, The sinews of his thighs are wrapped together,

40.he: עֲ֭צָמָיו אֲפִיקֵ֣י נְחוּשָׁ֑ה גְּ֝רָמָ֗יו כִּמְטִ֥יל בַּרְזֶֽל׃

lines.text: His bones are like tubes of bronze. His limbs are like bars of iron.
His bones [are] tubes of brass, His bones [are] as a bar of iron.

40.he: ה֭וּא רֵאשִׁ֣ית דַּרְכֵי־אֵ֑ל הָ֝עֹשׂוֹ יַגֵּ֥שׁ חַרְבּֽוֹ׃

lines.text: He is the chief of the ways of God. He who made him gives him his sword.
He [is] a beginning of the ways of God, His Maker bringeth nigh his sword;

40.he: כִּֽי־ב֭וּל הָרִ֣ים יִשְׂאוּ־ל֑וֹ וְֽכָל־חַיַּ֥ת הַ֝שָּׂדֶ֗ה יְשַֽׂחֲקוּ־שָֽׁם׃

lines.text: Surely the mountains produce food for him, where all the animals of the field play.
For food do mountains bear for him, And all the beasts of the field play there.

40.he: תַּֽחַת־צֶאֱלִ֥ים יִשְׁכָּ֑ב בְּסֵ֖תֶר קָנֶ֣ה וּבִצָּֽה׃

lines.text: He lies under the lotus trees, in the covert of the reed, and the marsh.
Under shades he lieth down, In a secret place of reed and mire.

40.he: יְסֻכֻּ֣הוּ צֶאֱלִ֣ים צִֽלֲל֑וֹ יְ֝סֻבּ֗וּהוּ עַרְבֵי־נָֽחַל׃

lines.text: The lotuses cover him with their shade. The willows of the brook surround him.
Cover him do shades, [with] their shadow, Cover him do willows of the brook.

40.he: הֵ֤ן יַעֲשֹׁ֣ק נָ֭הָר לֹ֣א יַחְפּ֑וֹז יִבְטַ֓ח ׀ כִּֽי־יָגִ֖יחַ יַרְדֵּ֣ן אֶל־פִּֽיהוּ׃

lines.text: Behold, if a river overflows, he doesn’t tremble. He is confident, though the Jordan swells even to his mouth.
Lo, a flood oppresseth — he doth not haste, He is confident though Jordan Doth come forth unto his mouth.

40.he: בְּעֵינָ֥יו יִקָּחֶ֑נּוּ בְּ֝מֽוֹקְשִׁ֗ים יִנְקָב־אָֽף׃

lines.text: Shall any take him when he is on the watch, or pierce through his nose with a snare?
Before his eyes doth [one] take him, With snares doth [one] pierce the nose?

40.he: תִּמְשֹׁ֣ךְ לִוְיָתָ֣ן בְּחַכָּ֑ה וּ֝בְחֶ֗בֶל תַּשְׁקִ֥יעַ לְשֹׁנֽוֹ׃

lines.text: “Can you draw out Leviathan with a fish hook, or press down his tongue with a cord?
Dost thou draw leviathan with an angle? And with a rope thou lettest down — his tongue?

40.he: הֲתָשִׂ֣ים אַגְמ֣וֹן בְּאַפּ֑וֹ וּ֝בְח֗וֹחַ תִּקּ֥וֹב לֶֽחֱיוֹ׃

lines.text: Can you put a rope into his nose, or pierce his jaw through with a hook?
Dost thou put a reed in his nose? And with a thorn pierce his jaw?

40.he: הֲיַרְבֶּ֣ה אֵ֭לֶיךָ תַּחֲנוּנִ֑ים אִם־יְדַבֵּ֖ר אֵלֶ֣יךָ רַכּֽוֹת׃

lines.text: Will he make many petitions to you, or will he speak soft words to you?
Doth he multiply unto thee supplications? Doth he speak unto thee tender things?

40.he: הֲיִכְרֹ֣ת בְּרִ֣ית עִמָּ֑ךְ תִּ֝קָּחֶ֗נּוּ לְעֶ֣בֶד עוֹלָֽם׃

lines.text: Will he make a covenant with you, that you should take him for a servant forever?
Doth he make a covenant with thee? Dost thou take him for a servant age-during?

40.he: הַֽתְשַׂחֶק־בּ֭וֹ כַּצִּפּ֑וֹר וְ֝תִקְשְׁרֶ֗נּוּ לְנַעֲרוֹתֶֽיךָ׃

lines.text: Will you play with him as with a bird? Or will you bind him for your girls?
Dost thou play with him as a bird? And dost thou bind him for thy damsels?

40.he: יִכְר֣וּ עָ֭לָיו חַבָּרִ֑ים יֶ֝חֱצ֗וּהוּ בֵּ֣ין כְּֽנַעֲנִֽים׃

lines.text: Will traders barter for him? Will they part him among the merchants?
(Feast upon him do companions, They divide him among the merchants!)

40.he: הַֽתְמַלֵּ֣א בְשֻׂכּ֣וֹת עוֹר֑וֹ וּבְצִלְצַ֖ל דָּגִ֣ים רֹאשֽׁוֹ׃

lines.text: Can you fill his skin with barbed irons, or his head with fish spears?
Dost thou fill with barbed irons his skin? And with fish-spears his head?

40.he: שִׂים־עָלָ֥יו כַּפֶּ֑ךָ זְכֹ֥ר מִ֝לְחָמָ֗ה אַל־תּוֹסַֽף׃

lines.text: Lay your hand on him. Remember the battle, and do so no more.
Place on him thy hand, Remember the battle — do not add!

41.he: הֵן־תֹּחַלְתּ֥וֹ נִכְזָ֑בָה הֲגַ֖ם אֶל־מַרְאָ֣יו יֻטָֽל׃

lines.text: Behold, the hope of him is in vain. Won’t one be cast down even at the sight of him?
Lo, the hope of him is found a liar, Also at his appearance is not one cast down?

41.he: לֹֽא־אַ֭כְזָר כִּ֣י יְעוּרֶ֑נּוּ וּמִ֥י ה֝֗וּא לְפָנַ֥י יִתְיַצָּֽב׃

lines.text: None is so fierce that he dare stir him up. Who then is he who can stand before me?
None so fierce that he doth awake him, And who [is] he before Me stationeth himself?

41.he: מִ֣י הִ֭קְדִּימַנִי וַאֲשַׁלֵּ֑ם תַּ֖חַת כָּל־הַשָּׁמַ֣יִם לִי־הֽוּא׃

lines.text: Who has first given to me, that I should repay him? Everything under the heavens is mine.
Who hath brought before Me and I repay? Under the whole heavens it [is] mine.

41.he: לא־אַחֲרִ֥ישׁ בַּדָּ֑יו וּדְבַר־גְּ֝בוּר֗וֹת וְחִ֣ין עֶרְכּֽוֹ׃

lines.text: “I will not keep silence concerning his limbs, nor his mighty strength, nor his goodly frame.
I do not keep silent concerning his parts, And the matter of might, And the grace of his arrangement.

41.he: מִֽי־גִ֭לָּה פְּנֵ֣י לְבוּשׁ֑וֹ בְּכֶ֥פֶל רִ֝סְנ֗וֹ מִ֣י יָבֽוֹא׃

lines.text: Who can strip off his outer garment? Who will come within his jaws?
Who hath uncovered the face of his clothing? Within his double bridle who doth enter?

41.he: דַּלְתֵ֣י פָ֭נָיו מִ֣י פִתֵּ֑חַ סְבִיב֖וֹת שִׁנָּ֣יו אֵימָֽה׃

lines.text: Who can open the doors of his face? Around his teeth is terror.
The doors of his face who hath opened? Round about his teeth [are] terrible.

41.he: גַּ֭אֲוָה אֲפִיקֵ֣י מָֽגִנִּ֑ים סָ֝ג֗וּר חוֹתָ֥ם צָֽר׃

lines.text: Strong scales are his pride, shut up together with a close seal.
A pride — strong ones of shields, Shut up — a close seal.

41.he: אֶחָ֣ד בְּאֶחָ֣ד יִגַּ֑שׁוּ וְ֝ר֗וּחַ לֹא־יָב֥וֹא בֵֽינֵיהֶֽם׃

lines.text: One is so near to another, that no air can come between them.
One unto another they draw nigh, And air doth not enter between them.

41.he: אִישׁ־בְּאָחִ֥יהוּ יְדֻבָּ֑קוּ יִ֝תְלַכְּד֗וּ וְלֹ֣א יִתְפָּרָֽדוּ׃

lines.text: They are joined to one another. They stick together, so that they can’t be pulled apart.
One unto another they adhere, They stick together and are not separated.

41.he: עֲֽ֭טִישֹׁתָיו תָּ֣הֶל א֑וֹר וְ֝עֵינָ֗יו כְּעַפְעַפֵּי־שָֽׁחַר׃

lines.text: His sneezing flashes out light. His eyes are like the eyelids of the morning.
His sneezings cause light to shine, And his eyes [are] as the eyelids of the dawn.

41.he: מִ֭פִּיו לַפִּידִ֣ים יַהֲלֹ֑כוּ כִּיד֥וֹדֵי אֵ֝֗שׁ יִתְמַלָּֽטוּ׃

lines.text: Out of his mouth go burning torches. Sparks of fire leap out.
Out of his mouth do flames go, sparks of fire escape.

41.he: מִ֭נְּחִירָיו יֵצֵ֣א עָשָׁ֑ן כְּד֖וּד נָפ֣וּחַ וְאַגְמֹֽן׃

lines.text: Out of his nostrils a smoke goes, as of a boiling pot over a fire of reeds.
Out of his nostrils goeth forth smoke, As a blown pot and reeds.

41.he: נַ֭פְשׁוֹ גֶּחָלִ֣ים תְּלַהֵ֑ט וְ֝לַ֗הַב מִפִּ֥יו יֵצֵֽא׃

lines.text: His breath kindles coals. A flame goes out of his mouth.
His breath setteth coals on fire, And a flame from his mouth goeth forth.

41.he: בְּֽ֭צַוָּארוֹ יָלִ֣ין עֹ֑ז וּ֝לְפָנָ֗יו תָּד֥וּץ דְּאָבָֽה׃

lines.text: There is strength in his neck. Terror dances before him.
In his neck lodge doth strength, And before him doth grief exult.

41.he: מַפְּלֵ֣י בְשָׂר֣וֹ דָבֵ֑קוּ יָצ֥וּק עָ֝לָ֗יו בַּל־יִמּֽוֹט׃

lines.text: The flakes of his flesh are joined together. They are firm on him. They can’t be moved.
The flakes of his flesh have adhered — Firm upon him — it is not moved.

41.he: לִ֭בּוֹ יָצ֣וּק כְּמוֹ־אָ֑בֶן וְ֝יָצ֗וּק כְּפֶ֣לַח תַּחְתִּֽית׃

lines.text: His heart is as firm as a stone, yes, firm as the lower millstone.
His heart [is] firm as a stone, Yea, firm as the lower piece.

41.he: מִ֭שֵּׂתוֹ יָג֣וּרוּ אֵלִ֑ים מִ֝שְּׁבָרִ֗ים יִתְחַטָּֽאוּ׃

lines.text: When he raises himself up, the mighty are afraid. They retreat before his thrashing.
From his rising are the mighty afraid, From breakings they keep themselves free.

41.he: מַשִּׂיגֵ֣הוּ חֶ֭רֶב בְּלִ֣י תָק֑וּם חֲנִ֖ית מַסָּ֣ע וְשִׁרְיָֽה׃

lines.text: If one attacks him with the sword, it can’t prevail; nor the spear, the dart, nor the pointed shaft.
The sword of his overtaker standeth not, Spear — dart — and lance.

41.he: יַחְשֹׁ֣ב לְתֶ֣בֶן בַּרְזֶ֑ל לְעֵ֖ץ רִקָּב֣וֹן נְחוּשָֽׁה׃

lines.text: He counts iron as straw; and bronze as rotten wood.
He reckoneth iron as straw, brass as rotten wood.

41.he: לֹֽא־יַבְרִיחֶ֥נּוּ בֶן־קָ֑שֶׁת לְ֝קַ֗שׁ נֶהְפְּכוּ־ל֥וֹ אַבְנֵי־קָֽלַע׃

lines.text: The arrow can’t make him flee. Sling stones are like chaff to him.
The son of the bow doth not cause him to flee, Turned by him into stubble are stones of the sling.

41.he: כְּ֭קַשׁ נֶחְשְׁב֣וּ תוֹתָ֑ח וְ֝יִשְׂחַ֗ק לְרַ֣עַשׁ כִּידֽוֹן׃

lines.text: Clubs are counted as stubble. He laughs at the rushing of the javelin.
As stubble have darts been reckoned, And he laugheth at the shaking of a javelin.

41.he: תַּ֭חְתָּיו חַדּ֣וּדֵי חָ֑רֶשׂ יִרְפַּ֖ד חָר֣וּץ עֲלֵי־טִֽיט׃

lines.text: His undersides are like sharp potsherds, leaving a trail in the mud like a threshing sledge.
Under him [are] sharp points of clay, He spreadeth gold on the mire.

41.he: יַרְתִּ֣יחַ כַּסִּ֣יר מְצוּלָ֑ה יָ֝֗ם יָשִׂ֥ים כַּמֶּרְקָחָֽה׃

lines.text: He makes the deep to boil like a pot. He makes the sea like a pot of ointment.
He causeth to boil as a pot the deep, The sea he maketh as a pot of ointment.

41.he: אַ֭חֲרָיו יָאִ֣יר נָתִ֑יב יַחְשֹׁ֖ב תְּה֣וֹם לְשֵׂיבָֽה׃

lines.text: He makes a path shine after him. One would think the deep had white hair.
After him he causeth a path to shine, One thinketh the deep to be hoary.

41.he: אֵֽין־עַל־עָפָ֥ר מָשְׁל֑וֹ הֶ֝עָשׂ֗וּ לִבְלִי־חָֽת׃

lines.text: On earth there is not his equal, that is made without fear.
There is not on the earth his like, That is made without terror.

41.he: אֵֽת־כָּל־גָּבֹ֥הַּ יִרְאֶ֑ה ה֝֗וּא מֶ֣לֶךְ עַל־כָּל־בְּנֵי־שָֽׁחַץ׃

lines.text: He sees everything that is high. He is king over all the sons of pride.”
Every high thing he doth see, He [is] king over all sons of pride.
Then Job answered Yahweh,
And Job answereth Jehovah and saith: —

42.he: ידעת כִּי־כֹ֣ל תּוּכָ֑ל וְלֹא־יִבָּצֵ֖ר מִמְּךָ֣ מְזִמָּֽה׃

lines.text: “I know that you can do all things, and that no purpose of yours can be restrained.
Thou hast known that [for] all things Thou art able, And not withheld from Thee is [any] device:

42.he: מִ֤י זֶ֨ה ׀ מַעְלִ֥ים עֵצָ֗ה בְּֽלִ֫י דָ֥עַת לָכֵ֣ן הִ֭גַּדְתִּי וְלֹ֣א אָבִ֑ין נִפְלָא֥וֹת מִ֝מֶּ֗נִּי וְלֹ֣א אֵדָֽע׃

lines.text: You asked, ‘Who is this who hides counsel without knowledge?’ therefore I have uttered that which I didn’t understand, things too wonderful for me, which I didn’t know.
'Who [is] this, hiding counsel without knowledge?' Therefore, I have declared, and understand not, Too wonderful for me, and I know not.
You said, ‘Listen, now, and I will speak; I will question you, and you will answer me.’
'Hear, I pray thee, and I — I do speak, I ask thee, and cause thou me to know.'
I had heard of you by the hearing of the ear, but now my eye sees you.
By the hearing of the ear I heard Thee, And now mine eye hath seen Thee.
Therefore I abhor myself, and repent in dust and ashes.”
Therefore do I loathe [it], And I have repented on dust and ashes.

42.he: וַיְהִ֗י אַחַ֨ר דִּבֶּ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־הַדְּבָרִ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה אֶל־אִיּ֑וֹב וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־אֱלִיפַ֣ז הַתֵּֽימָנִ֗י חָרָ֨ה אַפִּ֤י בְךָ֙ וּבִשְׁנֵ֣י רֵעֶ֔יךָ כִּ֠י לֹ֣א דִבַּרְתֶּ֥ם אֵלַ֛י נְכוֹנָ֖ה כְּעַבְדִּ֥י אִיּֽוֹב׃

lines.text: It was so, that after Yahweh had spoken these words to Job, Yahweh said to Eliphaz the Temanite, “My wrath is kindled against you, and against your two friends; for you have not spoken of me the thing that is right, as my servant Job has.

And it cometh to pass after Jehovah's speaking these words unto Job, that Jehovah saith unto Eliphaz the Temanite, 'Burned hath Mine anger against thee, and against thy two friends, because ye have not spoken concerning Me rightly, like My servant Job.

42.he: וְעַתָּ֡ה קְחֽוּ־לָכֶ֣ם שִׁבְעָֽה־פָרִים֩ וְשִׁבְעָ֨ה אֵילִ֜ים וּלְכ֣וּ ׀ אֶל־עַבְדִּ֣י אִיּ֗וֹב וְהַעֲלִיתֶ֤ם עוֹלָה֙ בַּֽעַדְכֶ֔ם וְאִיּ֣וֹב עַבְדִּ֔י יִתְפַּלֵּ֖ל עֲלֵיכֶ֑ם כִּ֧י אִם־פָּנָ֣יו אֶשָּׂ֗א לְבִלְתִּ֞י עֲשׂ֤וֹת עִמָּכֶם֙ נְבָלָ֔ה כִּ֠י לֹ֣א דִבַּרְתֶּ֥ם אֵלַ֛י נְכוֹנָ֖ה כְּעַבְדִּ֥י אִיּֽוֹב׃

lines.text: Now therefore, take to yourselves seven bulls and seven rams, and go to my servant Job, and offer up for yourselves a burnt offering; and my servant Job shall pray for you, for I will accept him, that I not deal with you according to your folly. For you have not spoken of me the thing that is right, as my servant Job has.”

And now, take to you seven bullocks and seven rams, and go ye unto My servant Job, and ye have caused a burnt-offering to ascend for you; and Job My servant doth pray for you, for surely his face I accept, so as not to do with you folly, because ye have not spoken concerning Me rightly, like My servant Job.

42.he: וַיֵּלְכוּ֩ אֱלִיפַ֨ז הַתֵּֽימָנִ֜י וּבִלְדַּ֣ד הַשּׁוּחִ֗י צֹפַר֙ הַנַּ֣עֲמָתִ֔י וַֽיַּעֲשׂ֔וּ כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר דִּבֶּ֥ר אֲלֵיהֶ֖ם יְהוָ֑ה וַיִּשָּׂ֥א יְהוָ֖ה אֶת־פְּנֵ֥י אִיּֽוֹב׃

lines.text: So Eliphaz the Temanite and Bildad the Shuhite and Zophar the Naamathite went, and did what Yahweh commanded them, and Yahweh accepted Job.
And they go — Eliphaz the Temanite, and Bildad the Shuhite, Zophar the Naamathite — and do as Jehovah hath spoken unto them; and Jehovah doth accept the face of Job.

42.he: וַֽיהוָ֗ה שָׁ֚ב אֶת־שבית אִיּ֔וֹב בְּהִֽתְפַּֽלְל֖וֹ בְּעַ֣ד רֵעֵ֑הוּ וַיֹּ֧סֶף יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֥ר לְאִיּ֖וֹב לְמִשְׁנֶֽה׃

lines.text: Yahweh turned the captivity of Job, when he prayed for his friends. Yahweh gave Job twice as much as he had before.
And Jehovah hath turned [to] the captivity of Job in his praying for his friends, and Jehovah doth add [to] all that Job hath — to double.

42.he: וַיָּבֹ֣אוּ אֵ֠לָיו כָּל־אֶחָ֨יו וְכָל־אחיתיו וְכָל־יֹדְעָ֣יו לְפָנִ֗ים וַיֹּאכְל֨וּ עִמּ֣וֹ לֶחֶם֮ בְּבֵיתוֹ֒ וַיָּנֻ֤דוּ לוֹ֙ וַיְנַחֲמ֣וּ אֹת֔וֹ עַ֚ל כָּל־הָ֣רָעָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־הֵבִ֥יא יְהוָ֖ה עָלָ֑יו וַיִּתְּנוּ־ל֗וֹ אִ֚ישׁ קְשִׂיטָ֣ה אֶחָ֔ת וְאִ֕ישׁ נֶ֥זֶם זָהָ֖ב אֶחָֽד׃

lines.text: Then came there to him all his brothers, and all his sisters, and all those who had been of his acquaintance before, and ate bread with him in his house. They comforted him, and consoled him concerning all the evil that Yahweh had brought on him. Everyone also gave him a piece of money, and everyone a ring of gold.

And come unto him do all his brethren, and all his sisters, and all his former acquaintances, and they eat bread with him in his house, and bemoan him, and comfort him concerning all the evil that Jehovah had brought upon him, and they gave to him each one kesitah, and each one ring of gold.

42.he: וַֽיהוָ֗ה בֵּרַ֛ךְ אֶת־אַחֲרִ֥ית אִיּ֖וֹב מֵרֵאשִׁת֑וֹ וַֽיְהִי־ל֡וֹ אַרְבָּעָה֩ עָשָׂ֨ר אֶ֜לֶף צֹ֗אן וְשֵׁ֤שֶׁת אֲלָפִים֙ גְּמַלִּ֔ים וְאֶֽלֶף־צֶ֥מֶד בָּקָ֖ר וְאֶ֥לֶף אֲתוֹנֽוֹת׃

lines.text: So Yahweh blessed the latter end of Job more than his beginning. He had fourteen thousand sheep, six thousand camels, one thousand yoke of oxen, and a thousand female donkeys.
And Jehovah hath blessed the latter end of Job more than his beginning, and he hath fourteen thousand of a flock, and six thousand camels, and a thousand pairs of oxen, and a thousand she-asses.
He had also seven sons and three daughters.
And he hath seven sons and three daughters;

42.he: וַיִּקְרָ֤א שֵׁם־הָֽאַחַת֙ יְמִימָ֔ה וְשֵׁ֥ם הַשֵּׁנִ֖ית קְצִיעָ֑ה וְשֵׁ֥ם הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֖ית קֶ֥רֶן הַפּֽוּךְ׃

lines.text: He called the name of the first, Jemimah; and the name of the second, Keziah; and the name of the third, Keren Happuch.
and he calleth the name of the one Jemima, and the name of the second Kezia, and the name of the third Keren-Happuch.

42.he: וְלֹ֨א נִמְצָ֜א נָשִׁ֥ים יָפ֛וֹת כִּבְנ֥וֹת אִיּ֖וֹב בְּכָל־הָאָ֑רֶץ וַיִּתֵּ֨ן לָהֶ֧ם אֲבִיהֶ֛ם נַחֲלָ֖ה בְּת֥וֹךְ אֲחֵיהֶֽם׃

lines.text: In all the land were no women found so beautiful as the daughters of Job. Their father gave them an inheritance among their brothers.
And there have not been found women fair as the daughters of Job in all the land, and their father doth give to them an inheritance in the midst of their brethren.

42.he: וַיְחִ֤י אִיּוֹב֙ אַֽחֲרֵי־זֹ֔את מֵאָ֥ה וְאַרְבָּעִ֖ים שָׁנָ֑ה וירא אֶת־בָּנָיו֙ וְאֶת־בְּנֵ֣י בָנָ֔יו אַרְבָּעָ֖ה דֹּרֽוֹת׃

lines.text: After this Job lived one hundred forty years, and saw his sons, and his sons’ sons, to four generations.
And Job liveth after this a hundred and forty years, and seeth his sons, and his sons' sons, four generations;
So Job died, being old and full of days.
and Job dieth, aged and satisfied [with] days.
